```ts
const trustedCertificates = ['-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----']

export const holder = new Agent({
  dependencies: agentDependencies,
  modules: {
    askar: new AskarModule({
      askar: NativeAskar,
      // In a real wallet, derive the key from a secret in the device's secure storage
      store: { id: 'holder', key: 'holder-key' },
    }),
    x509: new X509Module({ trustedCertificates }),
    openid4vc: new OpenId4VcModule(),
  },
})

await holder.initialize()
```

The holder verifies the credentials it receives, and later the requests of verifiers. To verify X.509 signatures, it needs the certificates, or root CAs, of the issuers and verifiers you trust. The Node.js example trusts the certificates from the [issuer](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/issuer.md) and [verifier](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/verifier.md) examples. See [Trusted issuers](https://credo.js.org/guides/dids-and-trust/trust.md). For storage and keys, see [Storage](https://credo.js.org/guides/agent-setup/storage.md) and [Key management](https://credo.js.org/guides/agent-setup/key-management.md). The React Native example uses [Askar](https://credo.js.org/guides/agent-setup/storage/askar.md), the default for mobile wallets.

## Resolve the offer

The wallet gets a credential offer URI from a QR code or a link. `resolveCredentialOffer` fetches the offer and the issuer metadata:

```ts
const resolvedCredentialOffer = await holder.openid4vc.holder.resolveCredentialOffer(credentialOffer)

// What to show the user: the issuer, the offered credentials and whether a code is needed
const issuerName = resolvedCredentialOffer.metadata.credentialIssuer.display?.[0]?.name
const offeredCredentials = Object.keys(resolvedCredentialOffer.offeredCredentialConfigurations)
const txCodeRequest =
  resolvedCredentialOffer.credentialOfferPayload.grants?.[preAuthorizedCodeGrantIdentifier]?.tx_code
```

Use the issuer metadata and `offeredCredentialConfigurations` to show the user who offers what. Display names, colors and claim labels are under `credential_metadata` of each configuration, or at its top level for issuers that implement draft 15. If `txCodeRequest` is defined, the issuer sent the user a code (by email, for example), and `description`, `length` and `input_mode` tell you what to ask for.

## Request an access token

In the pre-authorized code flow, exchange the code from the offer for an access token, with the transaction code the user entered:

```ts
// txCode is the code the user received from the issuer, if txCodeRequest is defined
const token = await holder.openid4vc.holder.requestToken({ resolvedCredentialOffer, txCode })
```

If the issuer supports DPoP, Credo creates the DPoP proof and returns its options in `token.dpop`. Pass them to the next calls. PKCE and DPoP need nothing else from you. Issuers that follow HAIP also ask for wallet attestations and key attestations, which your wallet gets from its wallet provider's backend. [Authorization and wallet security](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/authorization.md) covers those and offers that use the authorization code flow.

## Request the credentials

The issuer binds each credential to a key the holder controls. Credo calls your `credentialBindingResolver` once for each offered credential configuration, with what the issuer supports, and you return the keys to bind to:

```ts
const credentialBindingResolver: OpenId4VciCredentialBindingResolver = async ({ supportsJwk, proofTypes }) => {
  // The algorithms the issuer accepts for this credential that the wallet's KMS supports
  const algorithm = proofTypes.jwt?.supportedSignatureAlgorithms[0]
  if (!supportsJwk || !algorithm) throw new Error('The issuer does not support jwk binding with a jwt proof')

  const key = await holder.kms.createKeyForSignatureAlgorithm({ algorithm })
  return { method: 'jwk', keys: [Kms.PublicJwk.fromPublicJwk(key.publicJwk)] }
}
```

The resolver returns one of:

| Binding | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `{ method: 'jwk', keys }` | SD-JWT VC and mdoc. Keys from the agent's KMS. This is the default choice, and what HAIP requires. |
| `{ method: 'did', didUrls }` | W3C formats, which can't bind to a bare key. Verification methods of DIDs the agent created, when the issuer lists the DID method in `supportedDidMethods` or accepts all (`supportsAllDidMethods`). Not allowed for mdoc. |
| `{ method: 'attestation', keyAttestationJwt }` | Issuers that require key attestations. See [Authorization and wallet security](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/authorization.md#wallet-and-key-attestations). |

To receive a batch, return up to `issuerMaxBatchSize` keys of the same key type, and you get one credential instance per key.

Then request the credentials:

```ts
const { credentials, deferredCredentials } = await holder.openid4vc.holder.requestCredentials({
  resolvedCredentialOffer,
  accessToken: token.accessToken,
  cNonce: token.cNonce,
  dpop: token.dpop,
  credentialBindingResolver,
})
```

By default this requests every credential in the offer. Pass `credentialConfigurationIds` to request only some of them.

## Store the credentials

`requestCredentials` verifies each credential, including the issuer's signature and trust, but it doesn't store anything. Each result has a `record` that you store with the API for its format:

```ts
// requestCredentials verifies the credentials, but doesn't store them
for (const { record } of credentials) {
  if (record instanceof SdJwtVcRecord) await holder.sdJwtVc.store({ record })
  else if (record instanceof MdocRecord) await holder.mdoc.store({ record })
  else if (record instanceof W3cCredentialRecord) await holder.w3cCredentials.store({ record })
  else await holder.w3cV2Credentials.store({ record })
}
```

A batch arrives as one record with several instances in `record.credentialInstances`. If the issuer defers issuance, the credential is in `deferredCredentials` instead: call `requestDeferredCredentials` with its `transactionId` after `interval` seconds. If a credential has a `notificationId`, tell the issuer whether you stored it with `sendNotification` (`credential_accepted`, `credential_deleted` or `credential_failure`).

## Next steps

- [Presenting credentials](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/present.md): present the stored credentials to a verifier.
- [Authorization and wallet security](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/authorization.md): offers with the authorization code flow, and wallet and key attestations.
- [SD-JWT VC with OpenID4VC](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/sd-jwt-vc.md) and [mdoc with OpenID4VC](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/mdoc.md): format details for wallets.
- [Trusted issuers](https://credo.js.org/guides/dids-and-trust/trust.md): decide which issuers your wallet accepts.

# Issuance authorization and wallet security

> Choose an OpenID4VCI authorization flow, use Credo's authorization server, a chained or an external one, presentation during issuance, PKCE, DPoP, and wallet and key attestations.

This page is about issuance (OpenID4VCI): how an issuer decides who gets a credential beyond the pre-authorized code, and the protections that profiles such as HAIP ask for when a wallet requests credentials: PKCE, DPoP, wallet attestations and key attestations. Each section has an issuer part and a holder part. For the verifier side of security, such as signed requests and encrypted responses, see [Verifying credentials](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/verifier.md). [Issuing credentials](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/issuer.md) and [Receiving credentials](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/receive.md) explain the basics.

## Choose an authorization flow

| Flow | Who authenticates the user | Use when | Configure with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pre-authorized code | Your application, before it creates the offer | You already know the user, for example after a login on your website. | `preAuthorizedCodeFlowConfig`, see [Issuing credentials](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/issuer.md) |
| Presentation during issuance | Credo, which asks the holder to present a credential with OpenID4VP | The user proves who they are with a credential they already have, such as a PID. | `requirePresentationDuringIssuance` and `getVerificationSession` |
| Chained authorization server | Your identity provider, with Credo's authorization server in between | Users log in with your existing OpenID Connect provider. | `authorizationServerConfigs` with `type: 'chained'` |
| External authorization server | Your OAuth 2.0 authorization server, which holders use directly | You run an authorization server that already supports OpenID4VCI. | `authorizationServerConfigs` with `type: 'direct'` |

Start with the pre-authorized code. HAIP requires the authorization code flow, which the other three use. When users have to log in, prefer a chained authorization server over an external one: Credo's authorization server then still handles PAR, PKCE, DPoP and wallet attestations, which an external server has to implement itself.

Every credential configuration you offer with the authorization code flow needs a `scope`. Credo's built-in authorization server handles the first three flows, and requires pushed authorization requests (PAR).

## Security features

| Feature | Protects against | HAIP | Credo issuer default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PKCE | Another app redeeming an intercepted authorization code | Required, with `S256` | Off |
| DPoP | Someone else using a stolen access token. DPoP binds the token to a key of the holder. | Required | Off |
| Wallet attestation | Wallet apps you don't trust getting credentials. The wallet authenticates with an attestation from its wallet provider. | Issuers must authenticate wallets, usually with wallet attestations | Off |
| Key attestation | Credentials bound to keys without the protection you need, for example outside a secure element | Wallets must support them | Off, set per credential configuration |

For an issuer: turn on PKCE and DPoP. Require wallet and key attestations only when the wallets you issue to get them from their wallet provider, as in the EU Digital Identity Wallet ecosystem. Wallets without them can't get your credentials.

For a wallet: the Credo holder uses PKCE and DPoP automatically when the issuer supports them. Wallet and key attestations need a backend from your wallet provider, see [Wallet and key attestations](#wallet-and-key-attestations).

### Module and session options

Each requirement has a module option that applies to all issuance sessions, and an option per session: in `authorization` when you create an offer, or in the result of `getDynamicIssuanceSession` for wallet-initiated issuance.

| Module option | Per session | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pkceRequired` | `requirePkce` | `false` |
| `dpopRequired` | `requireDpop` | `false` |
| `walletAttestationsRequired` | `requireWalletAttestation` | `false` |

If you leave the per-session option out, the module option applies. `requirePkce: false` turns PKCE off for that session, even when the module option requires it. `requireDpop: false` and `requireWalletAttestation: false` fall back to the module option, so you can't turn a requirement of the module off for one session.

These options apply to Credo's authorization server. An external authorization server enforces its own rules. Credo only checks at the credential endpoint that the access token is bound with DPoP when the offer sets `requireDpop: true`.

## Presentation during issuance

The issuer asks the holder to present a credential, for example a PID, before it issues a new one. Credo creates the presentation request, verifies the response and only then gives the holder an authorization code:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant Holder
  participant Issuer as Credo issuer
  Holder->>Issuer: authorization challenge request (scope, PKCE, DPoP)
  Issuer-->>Holder: OpenID4VP request from getVerificationSession
  Holder->>Issuer: OpenID4VP response
  Holder->>Issuer: authorization challenge request with the presentation
  Issuer-->>Holder: authorization code
  Holder->>Issuer: token request and credential request
```

### Issuer

The issuer agent also needs the verifier part of the module, and a `getVerificationSession` callback:

:::issuer

```ts
const issuer = new Agent({
  config: { allowInsecureHttpUrls: true },
  dependencies: agentDependencies,
  modules: {
    ...issuerStorage, // Storage and key management, see Agent setup
    openid4vc: new OpenId4VcModule({
      app,
      issuer: {
        baseUrl: `${issuerUrl}/oid4vci`,
        credentialRequestToCredentialMapper,
        // Creates the OpenID4VP request for presentation during issuance
        getVerificationSession,
        // Require DPoP and PKCE for all issuance sessions. PKCE is off by default.
        dpopRequired: true,
        pkceRequired: true,
      },
      // Presentation during issuance uses the verifier of the same agent
      verifier: { baseUrl: `${issuerUrl}/oid4vp` },
    }),
  },
})
```

:::

The callback creates the OpenID4VP request when a holder starts the authorization. `scopes` are the requested scopes that match the offered credentials. Return the request together with the scopes it grants. The request needs a verifier record, here one with the same id as the issuer:

:::issuer

```ts
const getVerificationSession: OpenId4VciGetVerificationSession = async ({ agentContext, issuanceSession, scopes }) => {
  if (!scopes.includes('diploma')) throw new Error(`Unsupported scopes ${scopes.join(', ')}`)

  // Resolve the verifier from the agent context, so this also works for tenants
  const verifier = agentContext.resolve(OpenId4VcVerifierApi)
  const authorizationRequest = await verifier.createAuthorizationRequest({
    // A verifier with the same id as the issuer (created next to the issuer)
    verifierId: issuanceSession.issuerId,
    requestSigner: { method: 'x5c', x5c: [issuerCertificate] },
    dcql: {
      query: {
        credentials: [
          {
            id: 'pid',
            format: 'dc+sd-jwt',
            meta: { vct_values: ['urn:example:pid:1'] },
            claims: [{ path: ['given_name'] }, { path: ['family_name'] }],
          },
        ],
      },
    },
  })

  // The scopes that are granted once the presentation is verified
  return { ...authorizationRequest, scopes: ['diploma'] }
}
```

:::

Create the issuer with a `scope` per credential configuration, and an offer that requires the presentation. Leave `authorizationServerUrl` out (or set it to the issuer itself), as only Credo's authorization server handles this flow:

:::issuer

```ts
const issuerRecord = await issuer.openid4vc.issuer.createIssuer({
  issuerId: 'example-issuer',
  // Advertise DPoP support in the authorization server metadata
  dpopSigningAlgValuesSupported: [KnownJwaSignatureAlgorithms.ES256],
  credentialConfigurationsSupported: {
    diploma: {
      format: OpenId4VciCredentialFormatProfile.SdJwtDc,
      vct: 'urn:example:diploma:1',
      // Required for the authorization code flow
      scope: 'diploma',
      cryptographic_binding_methods_supported: ['jwk'],
      proof_types_supported: {
        jwt: { proof_signing_alg_values_supported: [KnownJwaSignatureAlgorithms.ES256] },
      },
    },
  },
})
await issuer.openid4vc.verifier.createVerifier({ verifierId: issuerRecord.issuerId })

const { credentialOffer } = await issuer.openid4vc.issuer.createCredentialOffer({
  issuerId: issuerRecord.issuerId,
  credentialConfigurationIds: ['diploma'],
  authorizationCodeFlowConfig: { requirePresentationDuringIssuance: true },
})
```

:::

The mapper receives the verified presentation in `verification`:

:::issuer

```ts
const credentialRequestToCredentialMapper: OpenId4VciCredentialRequestToCredentialMapper = async ({
  credentialConfiguration,
  holderBinding,
  verification,
}) => {
  if (credentialConfiguration.format !== OpenId4VciCredentialFormatProfile.SdJwtDc) {
    throw new Error(`Unsupported credential format ${credentialConfiguration.format}`)
  }
  if (holderBinding.bindingMethod !== 'jwk') throw new Error('Expected jwk holder binding')

  // The verified presentation from the authorization step
  const [pid] = verification?.dcql?.presentations.pid ?? []
  if (pid?.claimFormat !== ClaimFormat.SdJwtDc) throw new Error('Expected a verified PID presentation')

  return {
    type: 'credentials',
    format: ClaimFormat.SdJwtDc,
    credentials: holderBinding.keys.map((holder) => ({
      holder,
      issuer: { method: 'x5c', x5c: [issuerCertificate], issuer: issuerUrl },
      payload: {
        vct: credentialConfiguration.vct,
        name: `${pid.prettyClaims.given_name} ${pid.prettyClaims.family_name}`,
        degree: 'Bachelor of Science',
      },
      disclosureFrame: { _sd: ['name', 'degree'] },
    })),
  } satisfies OpenId4VciSignSdJwtCredentials
}
```

:::

### Holder

:::holder

```ts
const clientId = 'example-wallet'
const redirectUri = 'https://wallet.example.com/redirect'

const resolvedOffer = await holder.openid4vc.holder.resolveCredentialOffer(credentialOffer)
const authorization = await holder.openid4vc.holder.resolveOpenId4VciAuthorizationRequest(resolvedOffer, {
  clientId,
  redirectUri,
  scope: getScopesFromCredentialConfigurationsSupported(resolvedOffer.offeredCredentialConfigurations),
})
if (authorization.authorizationFlow !== OpenId4VciAuthorizationFlow.PresentationDuringIssuance) {
  throw new Error('Expected presentation during issuance')
}

// Present the PID with OpenID4VP
const presentationRequest = await holder.openid4vc.holder.resolveOpenId4VpAuthorizationRequest(
  authorization.openid4vpRequestUrl
)
if (!presentationRequest.dcql?.queryResult.can_be_satisfied) throw new Error('No matching credentials')
const presentation = await holder.openid4vc.holder.acceptOpenId4VpAuthorizationRequest({
  authorizationRequestPayload: presentationRequest.authorizationRequestPayload,
  dcql: { credentials: holder.openid4vc.holder.selectCredentialsForDcqlRequest(presentationRequest.dcql.queryResult) },
})
if (!presentation.ok) throw new Error('Presentation was rejected')

// Exchange the presentation for an authorization code
const { authorizationCode, dpop } = await holder.openid4vc.holder.retrieveAuthorizationCodeUsingPresentation({
  resolvedCredentialOffer: resolvedOffer,
  authSession: authorization.authSession,
  presentationDuringIssuanceSession: presentation.presentationDuringIssuanceSession,
  dpop: authorization.dpop,
})

const token = await holder.openid4vc.holder.requestToken({
  resolvedCredentialOffer: resolvedOffer,
  code: authorizationCode,
  clientId,
  redirectUri,
  // PKCE: proves this is the client that started the authorization
  codeVerifier: authorization.codeVerifier,
  // Keep using the same DPoP key
  dpop,
})

const { credentials } = await holder.openid4vc.holder.requestCredentials({
  resolvedCredentialOffer: resolvedOffer,
  ...token,
  clientId,
  credentialBindingResolver: async () => {
    const key = await holder.kms.createKey({ type: { kty: 'EC', crv: 'P-256' } })
    return { method: 'jwk', keys: [PublicJwk.fromPublicJwk(key.publicJwk)] }
  },
})
```

:::

`resolveOpenId4VciAuthorizationRequest` starts the authorization. `authorizationFlow` tells you whether the issuer wants a presentation or a browser redirect ([below](#external-authorization-servers)). Present the credential like any other OpenID4VP request: the result has `presentationDuringIssuanceSession`, which proves the presentation to the issuer. Pass `codeVerifier` (PKCE) and the `dpop` from the previous call to the token request.

## External authorization servers

### Issuer: chained

With a chained authorization server, holders talk to Credo's authorization server, which sends the user to your identity provider to log in. PAR, PKCE, DPoP and wallet attestations work as with Credo alone:

:::issuer

```ts
// Wallets use Credo's authorization server, which sends the user to your identity provider
const chainedIssuer = await issuer.openid4vc.issuer.createIssuer({
  issuerId: 'employee-chained',
  credentialConfigurationsSupported,
  authorizationServerConfigs: [
    {
      type: 'chained',
      issuer: 'https://idp.example.com',
      // Credo's client at the identity provider. Register
      // https://issuer.example.com/oid4vci/employee-chained/redirect as its redirect URI.
      clientAuthentication: { type: 'clientSecret', clientId: 'credo-issuer', clientSecret: 'secret' },
      // Credential scope -> scopes to request from the identity provider
      scopesMapping: { employee: ['openid', 'profile'] },
    },
  ],
})

await issuer.openid4vc.issuer.createCredentialOffer({
  issuerId: chainedIssuer.issuerId,
  credentialConfigurationIds: ['employee'],
  // Selects the chained authorization server
  authorizationCodeFlowConfig: { authorizationServerUrl: 'https://idp.example.com' },
})
```

:::

- Credo exchanges the code at your identity provider with `clientAuthentication`. Register `<baseUrl>/<issuerId>/redirect` as the redirect URI of that client.
- `scopesMapping` maps each credential scope to the scopes Credo requests from your identity provider. To decide per session instead, use the `getChainedAuthorizationRequestParameters` callback in the issuer module config.
- Set `redirectUris` to the redirect URIs of the wallets you accept. Without it, Credo accepts any redirect URI.

In the mapper, the token response of your identity provider, including an `id_token`, is in `issuanceSession.chainedIdentity.externalAccessTokenResponse`. A chained flow can't be combined with presentation during issuance.

### Issuer: direct

With a direct authorization server, Credo lists it in the issuer metadata, and holders use it directly:

:::issuer

```ts
// Wallets use your authorization server directly
const directIssuer = await issuer.openid4vc.issuer.createIssuer({
  issuerId: 'employee-direct',
  credentialConfigurationsSupported,
  authorizationServerConfigs: [
    {
      type: 'direct',
      issuer: 'https://auth.example.com',
      // Only needed if Credo has to introspect the access tokens
      clientAuthentication: { clientId: 'credo-issuer', clientSecret: 'secret' },
    },
  ],
})

await issuer.openid4vc.issuer.createCredentialOffer({
  issuerId: directIssuer.issuerId,
  credentialConfigurationIds: ['employee'],
  authorizationCodeFlowConfig: { authorizationServerUrl: 'https://auth.example.com' },
})
```

:::

Your authorization server must link the authorization to the offer through `issuer_state`, and handle PAR, PKCE, DPoP and wallet attestations itself if you need them. Credo verifies its access tokens at the credential endpoint, and only needs `clientAuthentication` for token introspection. For issuance without an offer, where the access token isn't linked to an issuance session, use `getDynamicIssuanceSession`.

### Holder

With both kinds, the holder opens the authorization URL in a browser and receives the code on its redirect URI:

:::holder

```ts
/**
 * `openAuthorizationUrl` opens the URL in a browser and resolves with the URL the
 * authorization server redirected to, for example using an in-app browser session.
 */
export async function receiveWithRedirect(
  credentialOffer: string,
  openAuthorizationUrl: (authorizationRequestUrl: string) => Promise<string>
) {
  const clientId = 'example-wallet'
  const redirectUri = 'https://wallet.example.com/redirect'

  const resolvedOffer = await holder.openid4vc.holder.resolveCredentialOffer(credentialOffer)
  const authorization = await holder.openid4vc.holder.resolveOpenId4VciAuthorizationRequest(resolvedOffer, {
    clientId,
    redirectUri,
    scope: getScopesFromCredentialConfigurationsSupported(resolvedOffer.offeredCredentialConfigurations),
  })
  if (authorization.authorizationFlow !== OpenId4VciAuthorizationFlow.Oauth2Redirect) {
    throw new Error('Expected a redirect to the authorization server')
  }

  const authorizationResponseRedirectUrl = await openAuthorizationUrl(authorization.authorizationRequestUrl)
  const { authorizationCode } = holder.openid4vc.holder.parseAuthorizationCodeFromAuthorizationResponse({
    authorizationResponseRedirectUrl,
    resolvedCredentialOffer: resolvedOffer,
  })

  const token = await holder.openid4vc.holder.requestToken({
    resolvedCredentialOffer: resolvedOffer,
    code: authorizationCode,
    clientId,
    redirectUri,
    codeVerifier: authorization.codeVerifier,
    // Bound to the DPoP key used for the pushed authorization request, if any
    dpop: authorization.dpop,
  })

  return holder.openid4vc.holder.requestCredentials({
    resolvedCredentialOffer: resolvedOffer,
    ...token,
    clientId,
    credentialBindingResolver: async () => {
      const key = await holder.kms.createKey({ type: { kty: 'EC', crv: 'P-256' } })
      return { method: 'jwk', keys: [PublicJwk.fromPublicJwk(key.publicJwk)] }
    },
  })
}
```

:::

The authorization request goes through PAR when the authorization server supports it. When the server supports PKCE, Credo adds it and returns the `codeVerifier` for the token request.

## PKCE and DPoP

### Issuer

PKCE ties the authorization code to the holder that started the authorization. Credo's authorization server doesn't require it by default. Turn it on with `pkceRequired: true`, as in the [full example](#full-example). Credo only supports the `S256` method. When a holder sends a code challenge, Credo always checks the code verifier, also for sessions that don't require PKCE.

DPoP binds the access token to a key of the holder. Enable it on the issuer record with `dpopSigningAlgValuesSupported`, as in the [presentation during issuance](#presentation-during-issuance) example: Credo only advertises DPoP when it's set. Require it with `dpopRequired` or `requireDpop`. When a holder uses DPoP in its first request, Credo requires it for the rest of that session.

### Holder

Credo creates the PKCE code challenge when the authorization server supports PKCE, and returns `codeVerifier`. Pass it to `requestToken`. Credo uses DPoP when the authorization server supports it. Each call returns the `dpop` options for the next call, as in the examples above. Spreading the token response into `requestCredentials` passes them on.

## Wallet and key attestations

A wallet attestation is a JWT from the wallet provider (the organization behind the wallet app) that says the wallet is a genuine instance of its app. The wallet uses it to authenticate to the authorization server ([OAuth 2.0 Attestation-Based Client Authentication](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-oauth-attestation-based-client-auth/)).

A key attestation lists keys of the wallet and how they're protected, such as in a secure element, with levels from ISO/IEC 18045 (`iso_18045_high`, `iso_18045_moderate`, `iso_18045_enhanced-basic`, `iso_18045_basic`). The issuer can require it before it binds credentials to those keys.

Both come from the wallet provider's backend. Credo doesn't create them.

### Issuer

Trust the wallet provider, for example with `getTrustedIssuersForVerification` in the agent config:

:::issuer

```ts
// Trust the wallet provider for wallet attestations and key attestations
const getTrustedIssuersForVerification: GetTrustedIssuersForVerification<
  VerificationSigner,
  OpenId4VcVerificationTypes
> = async (_agentContext, { verification }) => {
  if (verification.type === 'oauth2ClientAttestation' || verification.type === 'openId4VciKeyAttestation') {
    return { trustedIssuers: [{ method: 'x509', issuance: [walletProviderCertificate.toString('pem')] }] }
  }

  // Use the other trust configuration for everything else
  return undefined
}
```

:::

Credo checks attestations signed with an X.509 certificate against your trust configuration, and accepts DID-signed attestations unless you return a list of trusted DIDs. See [Trusted issuers](https://credo.js.org/guides/dids-and-trust/trust.md).

:::warning

Your trust configuration only applies to attestations signed with an `x5c` certificate chain or a DID. Credo accepts an attestation signed with a bare JWK (a `jwk` header) from anyone whose signature verifies, so it proves nothing about the wallet provider.

:::

Then require wallet attestations, advertise attestation-based client authentication (`clientAttestationSigningAlgValuesSupported` and `clientAttestationPopSigningAlgValuesSupported`), and set the key attestation requirements:

:::issuer

```ts
config: { allowInsecureHttpUrls: true, getTrustedIssuersForVerification },
dependencies: agentDependencies,
modules: {
  ...issuerStorage, // Storage and key management, see Agent setup
  openid4vc: new OpenId4VcModule({
    app,
    issuer: {
      baseUrl: `${issuerUrl}/oid4vci`,
      credentialRequestToCredentialMapper,
      // Every issuance session requires a wallet attestation
      walletAttestationsRequired: true,
    },
  }),
},
```

```ts
const issuerRecord = await issuer.openid4vc.issuer.createIssuer({
  issuerId: 'example-issuer',
  // Advertise attestation based client authentication
  clientAttestationSigningAlgValuesSupported: [KnownJwaSignatureAlgorithms.ES256],
  clientAttestationPopSigningAlgValuesSupported: [KnownJwaSignatureAlgorithms.ES256],
  batchCredentialIssuance: { batchSize: 2 },
  credentialConfigurationsSupported: {
    membership: {
      format: OpenId4VciCredentialFormatProfile.MsoMdoc,
      doctype: 'org.example.membership.1',
      cryptographic_binding_methods_supported: ['cose_key'],
      proof_types_supported: {
        jwt: {
          proof_signing_alg_values_supported: [KnownJwaSignatureAlgorithms.ES256],
          // The holder keys must be attested at this level
          key_attestations_required: {
            key_storage: [OpenId4VciKeyAttestationLevel.High],
            user_authentication: [OpenId4VciKeyAttestationLevel.High],
          },
        },
      },
    },
  },
})
```

:::

`key_attestations_required` on a proof type requires a key attestation with at least these levels. A higher level satisfies a lower one. Add an `attestation` proof type as well if wallets may send the key attestation as the proof itself.

By default Credo verifies a wallet attestation whenever a wallet sends one, and then requires it for the rest of the session. `ignoreWalletAttestationsWhenNotRequired` ignores attestations for sessions that don't require them. `clientAttestationPopChallengeRequired` makes wallets fetch a challenge for the proof of possession first.

The mapper gets the attested keys in `holderBinding.keys`, and the verified key attestation in `holderBinding.keyAttestation`:

:::issuer

```ts
const credentialRequestToCredentialMapper: OpenId4VciCredentialRequestToCredentialMapper = async ({
  credentialConfiguration,
  holderBinding,
}) => {
  if (credentialConfiguration.format !== OpenId4VciCredentialFormatProfile.MsoMdoc) {
    throw new Error(`Unsupported credential format ${credentialConfiguration.format}`)
  }
  if (holderBinding.bindingMethod !== 'jwk') throw new Error('Expected jwk holder binding')

  // Credo verified the key attestation, its trust and the required levels
  console.log('Attested key storage', holderBinding.keyAttestation?.payload.key_storage)

  return {
    type: 'credentials',
    format: ClaimFormat.MsoMdoc,
    // One credential per attested key
    credentials: holderBinding.keys.map(({ jwk }) => ({
      docType: credentialConfiguration.doctype,
      holderKey: jwk,
      issuerCertificate,
      validityInfo: { validUntil: new Date(Date.now() + 365 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000) },
      namespaces: { 'org.example.membership.1': { member_id: 'M-1234', issuing_country: 'NL' } },
    })),
  } satisfies OpenId4VciSignMdocCredentials
}
```

:::

### Holder

:::holder

```ts
const resolvedOffer = await holder.openid4vc.holder.resolveCredentialOffer(credentialOffer)

// Credo signs the attestation proof of possession with the key in the attestation's `cnf`
const token = await holder.openid4vc.holder.requestToken({
  resolvedCredentialOffer: resolvedOffer,
  walletAttestationJwt,
})

const { credentials } = await holder.openid4vc.holder.requestCredentials({
  resolvedCredentialOffer: resolvedOffer,
  ...token,
  clientId,
  credentialBindingResolver: ({ proofTypes }) => {
    if (!proofTypes.jwt?.keyAttestationsRequired) throw new Error('Expected key attestations to be required')

    // Without a nonce, Credo sends a jwt proof signed with the first attested key
    return { method: 'attestation', keyAttestationJwt }
  },
})
```

:::

Pass `walletAttestationJwt` to every call to the authorization server: `resolveOpenId4VciAuthorizationRequest`, `retrieveAuthorizationCodeUsingPresentation`, `requestToken` and `refreshToken`. Credo signs the proof of possession with the key in the attestation's `cnf`, so that key must be in the wallet's KMS.

When the issuer requires key attestations, `proofTypes.jwt.keyAttestationsRequired` (or `proofTypes.attestation`) says so, and the binding resolver must return `{ method: 'attestation', keyAttestationJwt }`. Binding to a DID isn't possible then. The attested keys must be in the wallet's KMS, with their KMS key id as `kid`, and you get one credential instance per attested key. Without a `nonce` in the key attestation, Credo sends a `jwt` proof signed with the first attested key. With the issuer's `cNonce` (passed to the resolver) as `nonce`, it sends the key attestation as an `attestation` proof.

## Full example

Presentation during issuance with PKCE and DPoP, in one process:

<details>
<summary>openid4vc-auth.ts</summary>

```ts
import { Agent, ClaimFormat, SdJwtVcRecord, type X509Certificate } from '@credo-ts/core'
import { KnownJwaSignatureAlgorithms, PublicJwk } from '@credo-ts/core/kms'
import { openid4vcBundle } from '@credo-ts/drizzle-storage/openid4vc'
import { agentDependencies } from '@credo-ts/node'
import {
  getScopesFromCredentialConfigurationsSupported,
  OpenId4VciAuthorizationFlow,
  OpenId4VciCredentialFormatProfile,
  type OpenId4VciCredentialRequestToCredentialMapper,
  type OpenId4VciGetVerificationSession,
  type OpenId4VciSignSdJwtCredentials,
  OpenId4VcModule,
  OpenId4VcVerifierApi,
} from '@credo-ts/openid4vc'
import express from 'express'
import { exampleStorage } from './example-storage.js'

const issuerUrl = 'http://localhost:4030'

// In-memory storage and keys, so the example leaves nothing behind
const issuerStorage = await exampleStorage([openid4vcBundle])
const holderStorage = await exampleStorage([openid4vcBundle])

// Created once the issuer agent is initialized (see below)
let issuerCertificate: X509Certificate

const getVerificationSession: OpenId4VciGetVerificationSession = async ({ agentContext, issuanceSession, scopes }) => {
  if (!scopes.includes('diploma')) throw new Error(`Unsupported scopes ${scopes.join(', ')}`)

  // Resolve the verifier from the agent context, so this also works for tenants
  const verifier = agentContext.resolve(OpenId4VcVerifierApi)
  const authorizationRequest = await verifier.createAuthorizationRequest({
    // A verifier with the same id as the issuer (created next to the issuer)
    verifierId: issuanceSession.issuerId,
    requestSigner: { method: 'x5c', x5c: [issuerCertificate] },
    dcql: {
      query: {
        credentials: [
          {
            id: 'pid',
            format: 'dc+sd-jwt',
            meta: { vct_values: ['urn:example:pid:1'] },
            claims: [{ path: ['given_name'] }, { path: ['family_name'] }],
          },
        ],
      },
    },
  })

  // The scopes that are granted once the presentation is verified
  return { ...authorizationRequest, scopes: ['diploma'] }
}

const credentialRequestToCredentialMapper: OpenId4VciCredentialRequestToCredentialMapper = async ({
  credentialConfiguration,
  holderBinding,
  verification,
}) => {
  if (credentialConfiguration.format !== OpenId4VciCredentialFormatProfile.SdJwtDc) {
    throw new Error(`Unsupported credential format ${credentialConfiguration.format}`)
  }
  if (holderBinding.bindingMethod !== 'jwk') throw new Error('Expected jwk holder binding')

  // The verified presentation from the authorization step
  const [pid] = verification?.dcql?.presentations.pid ?? []
  if (pid?.claimFormat !== ClaimFormat.SdJwtDc) throw new Error('Expected a verified PID presentation')

  return {
    type: 'credentials',
    format: ClaimFormat.SdJwtDc,
    credentials: holderBinding.keys.map((holder) => ({
      holder,
      issuer: { method: 'x5c', x5c: [issuerCertificate], issuer: issuerUrl },
      payload: {
        vct: credentialConfiguration.vct,
        name: `${pid.prettyClaims.given_name} ${pid.prettyClaims.family_name}`,
        degree: 'Bachelor of Science',
      },
      disclosureFrame: { _sd: ['name', 'degree'] },
    })),
  } satisfies OpenId4VciSignSdJwtCredentials
}

const app = express()
const issuer = new Agent({
  config: { allowInsecureHttpUrls: true },
  dependencies: agentDependencies,
  modules: {
    ...issuerStorage, // Storage and key management, see Agent setup
    openid4vc: new OpenId4VcModule({
      app,
      issuer: {
        baseUrl: `${issuerUrl}/oid4vci`,
        credentialRequestToCredentialMapper,
        // Creates the OpenID4VP request for presentation during issuance
        getVerificationSession,
        // Require DPoP and PKCE for all issuance sessions. PKCE is off by default.
        dpopRequired: true,
        pkceRequired: true,
      },
      // Presentation during issuance uses the verifier of the same agent
      verifier: { baseUrl: `${issuerUrl}/oid4vp` },
    }),
  },
})

const holder = new Agent({
  config: { allowInsecureHttpUrls: true },
  dependencies: agentDependencies,
  modules: {
    ...holderStorage,
    openid4vc: new OpenId4VcModule(),
  },
})

await issuer.initialize()
await holder.initialize()
const server = app.listen(4030)

// Self-signed certificate for the example. The SAN must match the host of `issuerUrl`.
issuerCertificate = await issuer.x509.createCertificate({
  authorityKey: PublicJwk.fromPublicJwk((await issuer.kms.createKey({ type: { kty: 'EC', crv: 'P-256' } })).publicJwk),
  issuer: { commonName: 'Credo example issuer', countryName: 'NL' },
  extensions: { subjectAlternativeName: { name: [{ type: 'dns', value: 'localhost' }] } },
})
issuer.x509.config.addTrustedCertificate(issuerCertificate)
holder.x509.config.addTrustedCertificate(issuerCertificate)

// The holder already has a PID, which it presents to get the diploma
const pidKey = await holder.kms.createKey({ type: { kty: 'EC', crv: 'P-256' } })
const pid = await issuer.sdJwtVc.sign({
  issuer: { method: 'x5c', x5c: [issuerCertificate], issuer: issuerUrl },
  holder: { method: 'jwk', jwk: PublicJwk.fromPublicJwk(pidKey.publicJwk) },
  payload: { vct: 'urn:example:pid:1', given_name: 'Erika', family_name: 'Mustermann' },
  disclosureFrame: { _sd: ['given_name', 'family_name'] },
})
await holder.sdJwtVc.store({
  record: new SdJwtVcRecord({ credentialInstances: [{ compactSdJwtVc: pid.compact, kmsKeyId: pidKey.keyId }] }),
})

const issuerRecord = await issuer.openid4vc.issuer.createIssuer({
  issuerId: 'example-issuer',
  // Advertise DPoP support in the authorization server metadata
  dpopSigningAlgValuesSupported: [KnownJwaSignatureAlgorithms.ES256],
  credentialConfigurationsSupported: {
    diploma: {
      format: OpenId4VciCredentialFormatProfile.SdJwtDc,
      vct: 'urn:example:diploma:1',
      // Required for the authorization code flow
      scope: 'diploma',
      cryptographic_binding_methods_supported: ['jwk'],
      proof_types_supported: {
        jwt: { proof_signing_alg_values_supported: [KnownJwaSignatureAlgorithms.ES256] },
      },
    },
  },
})
await issuer.openid4vc.verifier.createVerifier({ verifierId: issuerRecord.issuerId })

const { credentialOffer } = await issuer.openid4vc.issuer.createCredentialOffer({
  issuerId: issuerRecord.issuerId,
  credentialConfigurationIds: ['diploma'],
  authorizationCodeFlowConfig: { requirePresentationDuringIssuance: true },
})

const clientId = 'example-wallet'
const redirectUri = 'https://wallet.example.com/redirect'

const resolvedOffer = await holder.openid4vc.holder.resolveCredentialOffer(credentialOffer)
const authorization = await holder.openid4vc.holder.resolveOpenId4VciAuthorizationRequest(resolvedOffer, {
  clientId,
  redirectUri,
  scope: getScopesFromCredentialConfigurationsSupported(resolvedOffer.offeredCredentialConfigurations),
})
if (authorization.authorizationFlow !== OpenId4VciAuthorizationFlow.PresentationDuringIssuance) {
  throw new Error('Expected presentation during issuance')
}

// Present the PID with OpenID4VP
const presentationRequest = await holder.openid4vc.holder.resolveOpenId4VpAuthorizationRequest(
  authorization.openid4vpRequestUrl
)
if (!presentationRequest.dcql?.queryResult.can_be_satisfied) throw new Error('No matching credentials')
const presentation = await holder.openid4vc.holder.acceptOpenId4VpAuthorizationRequest({
  authorizationRequestPayload: presentationRequest.authorizationRequestPayload,
  dcql: { credentials: holder.openid4vc.holder.selectCredentialsForDcqlRequest(presentationRequest.dcql.queryResult) },
})
if (!presentation.ok) throw new Error('Presentation was rejected')

// Exchange the presentation for an authorization code
const { authorizationCode, dpop } = await holder.openid4vc.holder.retrieveAuthorizationCodeUsingPresentation({
  resolvedCredentialOffer: resolvedOffer,
  authSession: authorization.authSession,
  presentationDuringIssuanceSession: presentation.presentationDuringIssuanceSession,
  dpop: authorization.dpop,
})

const token = await holder.openid4vc.holder.requestToken({
  resolvedCredentialOffer: resolvedOffer,
  code: authorizationCode,
  clientId,
  redirectUri,
  // PKCE: proves this is the client that started the authorization
  codeVerifier: authorization.codeVerifier,
  // Keep using the same DPoP key
  dpop,
})

const { credentials } = await holder.openid4vc.holder.requestCredentials({
  resolvedCredentialOffer: resolvedOffer,
  ...token,
  clientId,
  credentialBindingResolver: async () => {
    const key = await holder.kms.createKey({ type: { kty: 'EC', crv: 'P-256' } })
    return { method: 'jwk', keys: [PublicJwk.fromPublicJwk(key.publicJwk)] }
  },
})

for (const { record } of credentials) {
  if (!(record instanceof SdJwtVcRecord)) throw new Error('Expected an SD-JWT VC')
  await holder.sdJwtVc.store({ record })
  console.log('Received diploma', record.firstCredential.prettyClaims.name, 'with DPoP', token.dpop !== undefined)
}

server.close()
await issuer.shutdown()
await holder.shutdown()
```

</details>

Wallet and key attestations, with a stand-in for the wallet provider:

<details>
<summary>openid4vc-auth-attestations.ts</summary>

```ts
import {
  Agent,
  ClaimFormat,
  type GetTrustedIssuersForVerification,
  JwsService,
  JwtPayload,
  MdocRecord,
  type VerificationSigner,
  type X509Certificate,
} from '@credo-ts/core'
import { KnownJwaSignatureAlgorithms, PublicJwk } from '@credo-ts/core/kms'
import { openid4vcBundle } from '@credo-ts/drizzle-storage/openid4vc'
import { agentDependencies } from '@credo-ts/node'
import {
  OpenId4VciCredentialFormatProfile,
  type OpenId4VciCredentialRequestToCredentialMapper,
  OpenId4VciKeyAttestationLevel,
  type OpenId4VciSignMdocCredentials,
  OpenId4VcModule,
  type OpenId4VcVerificationTypes,
} from '@credo-ts/openid4vc'
import express from 'express'
import { exampleStorage } from './example-storage.js'

const issuerUrl = 'http://localhost:4039'

// In-memory storage and keys, so the example leaves nothing behind
const holderStorage = await exampleStorage([openid4vcBundle])

const issuerStorage = await exampleStorage([openid4vcBundle])

// Created once the agents are initialized (see below)
let issuerCertificate: X509Certificate
let walletProviderCertificate: X509Certificate

// Trust the wallet provider for wallet attestations and key attestations
const getTrustedIssuersForVerification: GetTrustedIssuersForVerification<
  VerificationSigner,
  OpenId4VcVerificationTypes
> = async (_agentContext, { verification }) => {
  if (verification.type === 'oauth2ClientAttestation' || verification.type === 'openId4VciKeyAttestation') {
    return { trustedIssuers: [{ method: 'x509', issuance: [walletProviderCertificate.toString('pem')] }] }
  }

  // Use the other trust configuration for everything else
  return undefined
}

const credentialRequestToCredentialMapper: OpenId4VciCredentialRequestToCredentialMapper = async ({
  credentialConfiguration,
  holderBinding,
}) => {
  if (credentialConfiguration.format !== OpenId4VciCredentialFormatProfile.MsoMdoc) {
    throw new Error(`Unsupported credential format ${credentialConfiguration.format}`)
  }
  if (holderBinding.bindingMethod !== 'jwk') throw new Error('Expected jwk holder binding')

  // Credo verified the key attestation, its trust and the required levels
  console.log('Attested key storage', holderBinding.keyAttestation?.payload.key_storage)

  return {
    type: 'credentials',
    format: ClaimFormat.MsoMdoc,
    // One credential per attested key
    credentials: holderBinding.keys.map(({ jwk }) => ({
      docType: credentialConfiguration.doctype,
      holderKey: jwk,
      issuerCertificate,
      validityInfo: { validUntil: new Date(Date.now() + 365 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000) },
      namespaces: { 'org.example.membership.1': { member_id: 'M-1234', issuing_country: 'NL' } },
    })),
  } satisfies OpenId4VciSignMdocCredentials
}

const app = express()
const issuer = new Agent({
  config: { allowInsecureHttpUrls: true, getTrustedIssuersForVerification },
  dependencies: agentDependencies,
  modules: {
    ...issuerStorage, // Storage and key management, see Agent setup
    openid4vc: new OpenId4VcModule({
      app,
      issuer: {
        baseUrl: `${issuerUrl}/oid4vci`,
        credentialRequestToCredentialMapper,
        // Every issuance session requires a wallet attestation
        walletAttestationsRequired: true,
      },
    }),
  },
})

const holder = new Agent({
  config: { allowInsecureHttpUrls: true },
  dependencies: agentDependencies,
  modules: {
    ...holderStorage,
    openid4vc: new OpenId4VcModule(),
  },
})

await issuer.initialize()
await holder.initialize()
const server = app.listen(4039)

issuerCertificate = await issuer.x509.createCertificate({
  authorityKey: PublicJwk.fromPublicJwk((await issuer.kms.createKey({ type: { kty: 'EC', crv: 'P-256' } })).publicJwk),
  issuer: { commonName: 'Credo example issuer', countryName: 'NL' },
})
holder.x509.config.addTrustedCertificate(issuerCertificate)

// Stand-in for the wallet provider's backend, which attests genuine wallet instances and their keys.
// It is not part of Credo. The key lives in the holder agent to keep the example short.
walletProviderCertificate = await holder.x509.createCertificate({
  authorityKey: PublicJwk.fromPublicJwk((await holder.kms.createKey({ type: { kty: 'EC', crv: 'P-256' } })).publicJwk),
  issuer: { commonName: 'Example wallet provider', countryName: 'NL' },
})
function signByWalletProvider(typ: string, payload: Record<string, unknown>) {
  return holder.context.resolve(JwsService).createJwsCompact(holder.context, {
    keyId: walletProviderCertificate.publicJwk.keyId,
    payload: JwtPayload.fromJson({
      iat: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000),
      exp: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 300,
      ...payload,
    }),
    protectedHeaderOptions: {
      alg: KnownJwaSignatureAlgorithms.ES256,
      typ,
      x5c: [walletProviderCertificate.toString('base64')],
    },
  })
}

const clientId = 'example-wallet'
const walletInstanceKey = await holder.kms.createKey({ type: { kty: 'EC', crv: 'P-256' } })
const walletAttestationJwt = await signByWalletProvider('oauth-client-attestation+jwt', {
  iss: 'https://wallet-provider.example.com',
  sub: clientId,
  cnf: { jwk: PublicJwk.fromPublicJwk(walletInstanceKey.publicJwk).toJson() },
  wallet_name: 'Example wallet',
})

const attestedKeys = await Promise.all(
  [1, 2].map(async () =>
    PublicJwk.fromPublicJwk((await holder.kms.createKey({ type: { kty: 'EC', crv: 'P-256' } })).publicJwk)
  )
)
const keyAttestationJwt = await signByWalletProvider('key-attestation+jwt', {
  attested_keys: attestedKeys.map((key) => key.toJson()),
  key_storage: [OpenId4VciKeyAttestationLevel.High],
  user_authentication: [OpenId4VciKeyAttestationLevel.High],
})

const issuerRecord = await issuer.openid4vc.issuer.createIssuer({
  issuerId: 'example-issuer',
  // Advertise attestation based client authentication
  clientAttestationSigningAlgValuesSupported: [KnownJwaSignatureAlgorithms.ES256],
  clientAttestationPopSigningAlgValuesSupported: [KnownJwaSignatureAlgorithms.ES256],
  batchCredentialIssuance: { batchSize: 2 },
  credentialConfigurationsSupported: {
    membership: {
      format: OpenId4VciCredentialFormatProfile.MsoMdoc,
      doctype: 'org.example.membership.1',
      cryptographic_binding_methods_supported: ['cose_key'],
      proof_types_supported: {
        jwt: {
          proof_signing_alg_values_supported: [KnownJwaSignatureAlgorithms.ES256],
          // The holder keys must be attested at this level
          key_attestations_required: {
            key_storage: [OpenId4VciKeyAttestationLevel.High],
            user_authentication: [OpenId4VciKeyAttestationLevel.High],
          },
        },
      },
    },
  },
})

const { credentialOffer } = await issuer.openid4vc.issuer.createCredentialOffer({
  issuerId: issuerRecord.issuerId,
  credentialConfigurationIds: ['membership'],
  preAuthorizedCodeFlowConfig: {},
})

const resolvedOffer = await holder.openid4vc.holder.resolveCredentialOffer(credentialOffer)

// Credo signs the attestation proof of possession with the key in the attestation's `cnf`
const token = await holder.openid4vc.holder.requestToken({
  resolvedCredentialOffer: resolvedOffer,
  walletAttestationJwt,
})

const { credentials } = await holder.openid4vc.holder.requestCredentials({
  resolvedCredentialOffer: resolvedOffer,
  ...token,
  clientId,
  credentialBindingResolver: ({ proofTypes }) => {
    if (!proofTypes.jwt?.keyAttestationsRequired) throw new Error('Expected key attestations to be required')

    // Without a nonce, Credo sends a jwt proof signed with the first attested key
    return { method: 'attestation', keyAttestationJwt }
  },
})

for (const { record } of credentials) {
  if (!(record instanceof MdocRecord)) throw new Error('Expected an mdoc')
  await holder.mdoc.store({ record })
  console.log('Received', record.credentialInstances.length, 'mdoc instances')
}

server.close()
await issuer.shutdown()
await holder.shutdown()
```

</details>

# Verifying credentials

> Request and verify credential presentations with OpenID4VP and DCQL from a Credo verifier on Node.js.

This page covers verifying credentials with OpenID4VP from a Node.js agent: creating an authorization request with a DCQL query, choosing how the wallet responds and how the verifier identifies itself, and reading the verified claims. The examples request the SD-JWT VC issued in [Issuing credentials](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/issuer.md).

## Set up the verifier

Register `OpenId4VcModule` with a `verifier` configuration. [OpenID4VC](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc.md) explains the module options.

```ts
import { Agent, ClaimFormat, Kms, X509Module } from '@credo-ts/core'
import { agentDependencies } from '@credo-ts/node'
import {
  OpenId4VcModule,
  OpenId4VcVerificationSessionState,
  type OpenId4VcVerificationSessionStateChangedEvent,
  OpenId4VcVerifierEvents,
} from '@credo-ts/openid4vc'
import express from 'express'
import { issuerCertificate } from './openid4vc-issuer.js'

const verifierPort = 4021
const app = express()

export const verifier = new Agent({
  config: {
    // Allows the http://localhost URLs of this example. Never enable this in production.
    allowInsecureHttpUrls: true,
  },
  dependencies: agentDependencies,
  modules: {
    ...storage, // Storage and key management, see Agent setup
    // Certificates (or root CAs) of the credential issuers you accept
    x509: new X509Module({ trustedCertificates: [issuerCertificate] }),
    openid4vc: new OpenId4VcModule({
      app,
      verifier: { baseUrl: `http://localhost:${verifierPort}/oid4vp` },
    }),
  },
})

await verifier.initialize()
export const verifierServer = app.listen(verifierPort)
```

- `baseUrl` is the public URL of the verifier endpoints. Wallets fetch requests from it and post their responses to it.
- The verifier only accepts credentials from issuers it trusts. For X.509-signed credentials it needs the issuer certificates or their root CAs, here `issuerCertificate` from [Issuing credentials](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/issuer.md). Credentials signed with a DID are accepted from any DID unless you restrict them. See [Trusted issuers](https://credo.js.org/guides/dids-and-trust/trust.md).

## Create a verifier

A verifier record gives the verifier an id, used in its URLs, and the client metadata that wallets show to the user, such as `client_name` and `logo_uri`. Create it once and keep its `verifierId`. One agent can host several verifiers.

The verifier also needs a way to identify itself to wallets. The example signs its requests with a self-signed certificate:

```ts
const verifierRecord = await verifier.openid4vc.verifier.createVerifier({
  clientMetadata: { client_name: 'Example Verifier' },
})

const verifierKey = await verifier.kms.createKey({ type: { kty: 'EC', crv: 'P-256' } })

// Self-signed for this example. With x509_san_dns, the host of the verifier's
// baseUrl must be a DNS name in the certificate's subject alternative names.
export const verifierCertificate = await verifier.x509.createCertificate({
  authorityKey: Kms.PublicJwk.fromPublicJwk(verifierKey.publicJwk),
  issuer: { commonName: 'Example Verifier', countryName: 'NL' },
  extensions: { subjectAlternativeName: { name: [{ type: 'dns', value: 'localhost' }] } },
})
```

In production, use a certificate from a CA that wallets trust. [Client identifiers](#client-identifiers) explains the options.

## Create an authorization request

An authorization request describes the credentials and claims you want in a DCQL query:

```ts
export async function createEmployeeBadgeRequest() {
  const { authorizationRequest, verificationSession } = await verifier.openid4vc.verifier.createAuthorizationRequest({
    verifierId: verifierRecord.verifierId,
    requestSigner: { method: 'x5c', x5c: [verifierCertificate] },
    dcql: {
      query: {
        credentials: [
          {
            id: 'employee-badge',
            format: 'dc+sd-jwt',
            meta: { vct_values: ['urn:example:employee-badge:1'] },
            claims: [{ path: ['given_name'] }, { path: ['department'] }],
          },
        ],
      },
    },
  })

  // Show authorizationRequest as a QR code or link, and keep the session id to look up the result
  return { authorizationRequest, verificationSessionId: verificationSession.id }
}
```

Each credential query has an `id`, which you use to find the presentation in the result. `meta.vct_values` limits the query to SD-JWT VCs of that type, and `claims` lists the claims the wallet must disclose. [SD-JWT VC with OpenID4VC](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/sd-jwt-vc.md), [mdoc with OpenID4VC](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/mdoc.md) and [W3C VCs with OpenID4VC](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/w3c.md) show the queries for each format.

`authorizationRequest` is a URI such as `openid4vp://?client_id=...&request_uri=...`. Show it as a QR code when the wallet runs on another device, or as a link on the same device. For a same-device flow, also set `authorizationResponseRedirectUri`: the wallet opens this URL after it submits the response, so the user returns to your website or app. Include enough randomness in the URL (at least 128 bits) that nobody can guess it.

The request expires after 5 minutes. Change it per request with `expirationInSeconds`, or for all requests with `authorizationRequestExpirationInSeconds` in the verifier configuration.

### Version and query language

Use the default `version`, `v1` (OpenID4VP 1.0), with DCQL. Set `version` to `v1.draft24` or `v1.draft21` only for wallets that don't support OpenID4VP 1.0 yet. Only those drafts accept a DIF Presentation Exchange definition (`presentationExchange`) instead of DCQL, and Credo throws if you combine draft 21 with DCQL or transaction data. Don't use `clientIdPrefix: 'x509_hash'` with draft 21: Credo creates the request, but every response to it fails.

### Response modes

`responseMode` sets how the wallet returns the response:

| Response mode | How | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `direct_post.jwt` (default) | The wallet encrypts the response to a key Credo generates for each request and posts it to the verifier. | By default. HAIP requires it. |
| `direct_post` | The wallet posts the response without encryption. | Only for wallets that can't encrypt. With drafts 21 and 24, mdoc requests need `direct_post.jwt`. |
| `dc_api.jwt`, `dc_api` | The request and response go through the browser's [Digital Credentials API](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/dc-api/verifier.md). | For requests from a website. |

With `direct_post` and `direct_post.jwt`, Credo receives and verifies the response at its endpoint. You don't have to call anything.

### Client identifiers

The `requestSigner` decides how the verifier identifies itself, and which client identifier prefix the request uses:

| `requestSigner` | Client identifier | What you need |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{ method: 'x5c', x5c }` | `x509_san_dns:<host>` (default for `x5c`) | A certificate with the host of `baseUrl` as a DNS subject alternative name. |
| `{ method: 'x5c', x5c, clientIdPrefix: 'x509_hash' }` | `x509_hash:<certificate hash>` | A certificate. Its names don't have to match your host. |
| `{ method: 'did', didUrl }` | `decentralized_identifier:<did>` | A DID created by the agent, with `didUrl` pointing to the signing key. |
| `{ method: 'none' }` | `redirect_uri:<response URL>` | Nothing. The request isn't signed. |

In production, sign requests with an X.509 certificate from a CA that wallets trust, so wallets can show the user who is asking. Use `x509_hash` for wallets that follow HAIP, which requires it, and `x509_san_dns` for wallets that only support that prefix. Use `did` only in ecosystems where wallets trust verifier DIDs. Unsigned requests (`none`) let anyone pretend to be your verifier, and HAIP doesn't allow them. Use them only for development.

For `x5c`, `baseUrl` must use HTTPS. Put the certificate of the signing key first, followed by any intermediate certificates. The first certificate needs the KMS key id of its key: `agent.x509.createCertificate` sets it, and for a certificate you load yourself, set `certificate.keyId`. Credo doesn't support the `verifier_attestation`, `openid_federation`, `pre-registered` and `https` prefixes.

## Track verification sessions

Each request creates a verification session:

```ts
verifier.events.on<OpenId4VcVerificationSessionStateChangedEvent>(
  OpenId4VcVerifierEvents.VerificationSessionStateChanged,
  ({ payload: { verificationSession } }) => {
    if (verificationSession.state === OpenId4VcVerificationSessionState.ResponseVerified) {
      console.log(`Verification session ${verificationSession.id} verified`)
    } else if (verificationSession.state === OpenId4VcVerificationSessionState.Error) {
      console.error(`Verification session ${verificationSession.id} failed: ${verificationSession.errorMessage}`)
    }
  }
)
```

| State | When |
| --- | --- |
| `RequestCreated` | You created the request. |
| `RequestUriRetrieved` | The wallet fetched the request. |
| `ResponseVerified` | The wallet responded and all presentations passed verification. |
| `Error` | Verification failed, or the user declined and the wallet sent an error response. `errorMessage` says why. |

A verifier website usually shows the QR code and polls its backend, which checks the session with `getVerificationSessionById`.

## Read the verified result

When the session reaches `ResponseVerified`, Credo has already checked the signatures, the holder binding, the nonce and audience, and the issuer's trust. Get the presentations:

```ts
export async function getEmployeeBadgeClaims(verificationSessionId: string) {
  // Throws unless the session is in state ResponseVerified
  const { dcql } = await verifier.openid4vc.verifier.getVerifiedAuthorizationResponse(verificationSessionId)

  const [presentation] = dcql?.presentations['employee-badge'] ?? []
  if (presentation?.claimFormat !== ClaimFormat.SdJwtDc) throw new Error('Expected an SD-JWT VC presentation')

  // Only the claims the holder disclosed, plus the always-visible ones like vct and iat
  return presentation.prettyClaims
}
```

`dcql.presentations` has an entry per credential query id, with one presentation per credential the wallet shared (more than one only if the query sets `multiple: true`). For SD-JWT VC, `prettyClaims` holds the disclosed claims; the format pages show how to read the other formats. `dcql.presentationResult` is the DCQL result for the whole query, for example to see which `credential_sets` were satisfied.

## Next steps

- [Presenting credentials](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/present.md): the holder side of this flow.
- [Digital Credentials API](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/dc-api/verifier.md): request credentials through the browser.
- [Trusted issuers](https://credo.js.org/guides/dids-and-trust/trust.md): decide which issuers you accept.

# Presenting credentials

> Present stored credentials to a verifier with OpenID4VP from a Credo wallet on Node.js or React Native, with DCQL or Presentation Exchange.

This page covers the holder side of OpenID4VP: resolving a verifier's authorization request, showing the user what it asks for, and sending the response. It uses the holder agent from [Receiving credentials](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/receive.md#set-up-the-holder), which also trusts the verifier's certificate, and the SD-JWT VC it received there. The verifier side is in [Verifying credentials](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/verifier.md).

## Resolve the authorization request

A verifier sends an authorization request as a QR code or link (`openid4vp://...`). `resolveOpenId4VpAuthorizationRequest` fetches the request, verifies its signature and finds the stored credentials that match its DCQL query:

```ts
const resolvedRequest = await holder.openid4vc.holder.resolveOpenId4VpAuthorizationRequest(authorizationRequest)

// Who is asking, e.g. prefix 'x509_san_dns' and client id 'x509_san_dns:localhost'
const { clientIdPrefix, effectiveClientId } = resolvedRequest.verifier

const queryResult = resolvedRequest.dcql?.queryResult
if (!queryResult?.can_be_satisfied) throw new Error('Your stored credentials do not match the request')

// For each credential query: the matching credentials and the claims they would disclose
for (const [queryId, match] of Object.entries(queryResult.credential_matches)) {
  if (!match.success) continue
  for (const { record, claims } of match.valid_credentials) {
    console.log(queryId, record.type, claims.valid_claim_sets[0].output)
  }
}
```

`resolvedRequest.verifier` tells you who is asking. With `x509_san_dns` or `x509_hash` the request was signed with a certificate that the holder trusts, and resolving throws if it doesn't. With `decentralized_identifier` it was signed with a DID. With `redirect_uri` the request isn't signed, so anyone could have created it: show the user that the verifier is unverified, or reject such requests.

`queryResult.can_be_satisfied` is `false` when the holder doesn't have the credentials the verifier asks for. Otherwise `credential_matches` lists, for each credential query, the matching credentials and the claims each would disclose. Use it to show the user what they're about to share.

## Submit the response

After the user agrees, select the credentials and send the response:

```ts
// Picks the first matching credential for each query. Ask the user for consent before you submit.
const credentials = holder.openid4vc.holder.selectCredentialsForDcqlRequest(queryResult)

const result = await holder.openid4vc.holder.acceptOpenId4VpAuthorizationRequest({
  authorizationRequestPayload: resolvedRequest.authorizationRequestPayload,
  dcql: { credentials },
})

if (!result.ok) throw new Error(`The verifier rejected the response: ${JSON.stringify(result.serverResponse.body)}`)
```

`selectCredentialsForDcqlRequest` picks the first matching credential for each query and discloses only the requested claims. For credentials received in a batch it uses an unused instance while there is one (`useMode`, default `NewOrFirst`).

Credo posts the response to the verifier's response endpoint. If the verifier rejects it, the call doesn't throw: `result.ok` is `false` and `result.serverResponse` holds the verifier's answer. `result.redirectUri` is set when the verifier wants the user to continue on its website or app. Open it in the browser.

Verifiers that use an OpenID4VP draft may send a DIF Presentation Exchange definition instead of a DCQL query. Then `resolvedRequest.presentationExchange` is set instead of `dcql`: select with `selectCredentialsForPresentationExchangeRequest` and pass `presentationExchange: { credentials }` when accepting. For requests that include transaction data, see [SD-JWT VC with OpenID4VC](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/sd-jwt-vc.md#sign-transaction-data). For requests from a website through the browser, see [Digital Credentials API](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/dc-api/wallet.md).

## Next steps

- [SD-JWT VC with OpenID4VC](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/sd-jwt-vc.md) and [mdoc with OpenID4VC](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/mdoc.md): format details, such as transaction data.
- [Digital Credentials API](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/dc-api/wallet.md): answer requests that a website sends through the browser.
- [Trusted issuers](https://credo.js.org/guides/dids-and-trust/trust.md): decide which verifiers your wallet accepts.

# SD-JWT VC with OpenID4VC

> Issue, receive and verify SD-JWT VCs over OpenID4VCI and OpenID4VP with Credo, including selective disclosure with DCQL and transaction data.

This page covers what is specific to SD-JWT VC in OpenID4VC, in the order of the flow. Issuance covers the issuer's credential configuration and signing, and what the holder stores. Presentation covers the verifier's DCQL query, transaction data and the result. [Issuing credentials](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/issuer.md), [Receiving credentials](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/receive.md), [Presenting credentials](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/present.md) and [Verifying credentials](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/verifier.md) explain the flow itself, and [SD-JWT VC](https://credo.js.org/guides/credential-formats/sd-jwt-vc.md) explains the format.

Use SD-JWT VC by default. HAIP requires SD-JWT VC or mdoc, and the EU PID uses SD-JWT VC.

## Issuance

### Configure the credential

Add a `dc+sd-jwt` entry to the `credentialConfigurationsSupported` of the issuer:

:::issuer

```ts
const credentialConfigurationsSupported = {
  'identity-sd-jwt': {
    format: OpenId4VciCredentialFormatProfile.SdJwtDc,
    vct: 'urn:example:identity:1',
    scope: 'identity',
    cryptographic_binding_methods_supported: ['jwk'],
    credential_signing_alg_values_supported: [KnownJwaSignatureAlgorithms.ES256],
    proof_types_supported: {
      jwt: { proof_signing_alg_values_supported: [KnownJwaSignatureAlgorithms.ES256] },
    },
    credential_metadata: {
      display: [{ name: 'Identity card', locale: 'en', background_color: '#1d3557', text_color: '#ffffff' }],
      claims: [
        { path: ['given_name'], display: [{ name: 'Given name', locale: 'en' }] },
        { path: ['family_name'], display: [{ name: 'Family name', locale: 'en' }] },
        { path: ['birthdate'], display: [{ name: 'Date of birth', locale: 'en' }] },
        { path: ['address', 'country'], display: [{ name: 'Country', locale: 'en' }] },
      ],
    },
  },
} satisfies Record<string, OpenId4VciCredentialConfigurationSupportedWithFormats>
```

:::

- `vct` is the credential type. Verifiers request credentials by it, and Credo checks that every credential the mapper returns has this `vct`. If it's an HTTPS URL, a Credo holder fetches the type metadata from it when it receives the credential and keeps it on the record (`record.typeMetadata`).
- `cryptographic_binding_methods_supported` decides what the holder binds the credential to: `jwk` for a key (the default choice, and what HAIP requires), or DID methods such as `did:key`.

`credential_metadata` holds what wallets show: the card in `display` and a label per claim in `claims`, where `path` points into the credential. Add a `scope` if you offer the credential through the [authorization code flow](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/authorization.md).

Wallets that implement older drafts use the format `vc+sd-jwt`. Credo accepts it as SD-JWT VC when the configuration has a `vct`, and signs the credential with `vc+sd-jwt` as `typ`. Without a `vct`, `vc+sd-jwt` means a W3C VCDM 2.0 credential, see [W3C VCs with OpenID4VC](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/w3c.md).

### Sign the credential

The mapper returns the SD-JWT VC sign options, one entry for each holder key:

:::issuer

```ts
const credentialRequestToCredentialMapper: OpenId4VciCredentialRequestToCredentialMapper = async ({
  credentialConfiguration,
  holderBinding,
  issuanceSession,
}) => {
  if (credentialConfiguration.format !== OpenId4VciCredentialFormatProfile.SdJwtDc) {
    throw new Error(`Unsupported credential format ${credentialConfiguration.format}`)
  }
  if (holderBinding.bindingMethod !== 'jwk') throw new Error('Only jwk holder binding is supported')

  // Look up the data for this user, e.g. based on the issuance metadata of the offer
  const { userId } = issuanceSession.issuanceMetadata ?? {}
  if (userId !== 'user-123') throw new Error('Unknown user')

  return {
    type: 'credentials',
    format: ClaimFormat.SdJwtDc,
    // One credential per holder key (more than one with batch issuance)
    credentials: holderBinding.keys.map((holder) => ({
      holder,
      issuer: { method: 'x5c', x5c: [issuerCertificate], issuer: issuerUrl },
      payload: {
        vct: credentialConfiguration.vct,
        given_name: 'Erika',
        family_name: 'Mustermann',
        birthdate: '1984-01-26',
        address: { street_address: 'Heidestraße 17', locality: 'Köln', country: 'DE' },
      },
      disclosureFrame: {
        _sd: ['given_name', 'family_name', 'birthdate'],
        address: { _sd: ['street_address', 'locality', 'country'] },
      },
    })),
  } satisfies OpenId4VciSignSdJwtCredentials
}
```

:::

- `payload.vct` must be the `vct` of the configuration. Credo adds `iat`, and sets `iss` and `cnf` from `issuer` and `holder`.
- `issuer` signs with an X.509 certificate chain (`x5c`, leaf first) or a DID (`{ method: 'did', didUrl }`, for a DID created in this agent). The optional `issuer` URL becomes the `iss` claim and must match a DNS or URI subject alternative name of the leaf certificate.
- `disclosureFrame` lists in `_sd` the claims the holder can disclose one by one. Claims that aren't listed are always visible. [SD-JWT VC](https://credo.js.org/guides/credential-formats/sd-jwt-vc.md) explains nested frames and decoys.

For revocation, add a `status` claim to the payload. See [Status lists](https://credo.js.org/guides/credential-formats/status-lists.md).

### Trust the issuer

The holder verifies each credential when it receives it, and the verifier verifies it again in the presentation. For an X.509-signed credential, both need the issuer certificate or its root CA:

```ts
// Both the holder and the verifier only accept credentials from issuers they trust
holder.x509.config.addTrustedCertificate(issuerCertificate)
verifier.x509.config.addTrustedCertificate(issuerCertificate)
```

DID-signed credentials are accepted from any DID unless you configure trusted issuers. [Trusted issuers](https://credo.js.org/guides/dids-and-trust/trust.md) covers both, and how to decide per verification.

### Receive and store

The holder side is the same as for other formats. Only the record type differs:

:::holder

```ts
const resolvedOffer = await holder.openid4vc.holder.resolveCredentialOffer(credentialOffer)
const token = await holder.openid4vc.holder.requestToken({ resolvedCredentialOffer: resolvedOffer })

const { credentials } = await holder.openid4vc.holder.requestCredentials({
  resolvedCredentialOffer: resolvedOffer,
  ...token,
  credentialBindingResolver: async ({ proofTypes }) => {
    const algorithm = proofTypes.jwt?.supportedSignatureAlgorithms[0]
    if (!algorithm) throw new Error('No supported proof of possession algorithm')

    const key = await holder.kms.createKeyForSignatureAlgorithm({ algorithm })
    return { method: 'jwk', keys: [PublicJwk.fromPublicJwk(key.publicJwk)] }
  },
})

for (const { record } of credentials) {
  if (!(record instanceof SdJwtVcRecord)) throw new Error('Expected an SD-JWT VC')

  await holder.sdJwtVc.store({ record })
  console.log('Stored SD-JWT VC with claims', record.firstCredential.prettyClaims)
}
```

:::

`requestCredentials` doesn't store anything. The `SdJwtVcRecord` has one instance per credential the issuer returned, so a batch ends up in one record. `record.firstCredential.prettyClaims` has all claims, decoded.

## Presentation

The verifier needs the same trust configuration as the holder, see [Trust the issuer](#trust-the-issuer).

### Request claims with DCQL

The verifier asks for SD-JWT VCs by `vct` and lists the claims it needs:

:::verifier

```ts
const { authorizationRequest, verificationSession } = await verifier.openid4vc.verifier.createAuthorizationRequest({
  verifierId: verifierRecord.verifierId,
  requestSigner: { method: 'none' },
  dcql: {
    query: {
      credentials: [
        {
          id: 'identity',
          format: 'dc+sd-jwt',
          meta: { vct_values: ['urn:example:identity:1'] },
          // Only these claims are disclosed, the others stay hidden
          claims: [{ path: ['given_name'] }, { path: ['address', 'country'] }],
        },
      ],
    },
  },
  transactionData: [
    {
      type: 'urn:example:transaction:age-check',
      credential_ids: ['identity'],
      transaction_data_hashes_alg: ['sha-256'],
    },
  ],
})
```

:::

- `format` is `dc+sd-jwt`. `meta.vct_values` also matches credentials whose type metadata extends one of the values.
- Each entry in `claims` has a `path` into the credential. `null` in a path selects all items of an array, and a number selects one item. Add `values` to only accept certain values, and `claim_sets` to accept alternative combinations of claims.

The wallet discloses only the requested claims. Claims the issuer didn't make selectively disclosable are always in the presentation.

### Add transaction data

A verifier can ask the holder to sign over extra data, such as the details of a payment, as part of the presentation. The request above has one `transactionData` entry. `type` is defined by your application, and `credential_ids` lists the DCQL credential query ids that may sign it. `transaction_data_hashes_alg` defaults to `sha-256`. Credo supports transaction data for SD-JWT VC only, and not with OpenID4VP draft 21.

### Sign transaction data

`resolvedRequest.transactionData` lists each entry with the credentials that can sign it. Show the user what they're signing, and pass one credential id per entry when you accept:

:::holder

```ts
const resolvedRequest = await holder.openid4vc.holder.resolveOpenId4VpAuthorizationRequest(authorizationRequest)
if (!resolvedRequest.dcql?.queryResult.can_be_satisfied) throw new Error('No matching credentials')

const result = await holder.openid4vc.holder.acceptOpenId4VpAuthorizationRequest({
  authorizationRequestPayload: resolvedRequest.authorizationRequestPayload,
  dcql: { credentials: holder.openid4vc.holder.selectCredentialsForDcqlRequest(resolvedRequest.dcql.queryResult) },
  // Sign each transaction data entry with one of the credentials it lists
  transactionData: resolvedRequest.transactionData?.map(({ matchedCredentialIds }) => ({
    credentialId: matchedCredentialIds[0],
  })),
})
if (!result.ok) throw new Error(`Verifier rejected the presentation: ${result.serverResponse.status}`)
```

:::

The holder includes a hash of each entry in the key binding JWT.

### Read the disclosed claims

After the session reaches `ResponseVerified`, the presentation is an `SdJwtVc`:

:::verifier

```ts
const { dcql, transactionData } = await verifier.openid4vc.verifier.getVerifiedAuthorizationResponse(
  verificationSession.id
)

const [presentation] = dcql?.presentations.identity ?? []
if (presentation?.claimFormat !== ClaimFormat.SdJwtDc) throw new Error('Expected an SD-JWT VC presentation')

// Only the disclosed claims (plus the always visible ones, like vct and iss)
console.log('Disclosed claims', presentation.prettyClaims)
console.log(
  'Signed transaction data',
  transactionData?.map(({ decoded }) => decoded.type)
)
```

:::

`prettyClaims` has the disclosed claims and the claims that are always visible, such as `vct`, `iss` and `cnf`. `payload` has the raw JWT payload. `transactionData` has an entry per transaction data entry, with the decoded entry, the credential query id that signed it, and the hashes Credo checked.

## Full example

The issuer, holder and verifier from this page in one process:

<details>
<summary>openid4vc-sd-jwt-vc.ts</summary>

```ts
import { Agent, ClaimFormat, SdJwtVcRecord, type X509Certificate } from '@credo-ts/core'
import { KnownJwaSignatureAlgorithms, PublicJwk } from '@credo-ts/core/kms'
import { openid4vcBundle } from '@credo-ts/drizzle-storage/openid4vc'
import { agentDependencies } from '@credo-ts/node'
import {
  type OpenId4VciCredentialConfigurationSupportedWithFormats,
  OpenId4VciCredentialFormatProfile,
  type OpenId4VciCredentialRequestToCredentialMapper,
  type OpenId4VciSignSdJwtCredentials,
  OpenId4VcModule,
} from '@credo-ts/openid4vc'
import express from 'express'
import { exampleStorage } from './example-storage.js'

const issuerUrl = 'http://localhost:4031'
const verifierUrl = 'http://localhost:4032'

// In-memory storage and keys, so the example leaves nothing behind
const issuerStorage = await exampleStorage([openid4vcBundle])
const verifierStorage = await exampleStorage([openid4vcBundle])
const holderStorage = await exampleStorage([openid4vcBundle])

const credentialConfigurationsSupported = {
  'identity-sd-jwt': {
    format: OpenId4VciCredentialFormatProfile.SdJwtDc,
    vct: 'urn:example:identity:1',
    scope: 'identity',
    cryptographic_binding_methods_supported: ['jwk'],
    credential_signing_alg_values_supported: [KnownJwaSignatureAlgorithms.ES256],
    proof_types_supported: {
      jwt: { proof_signing_alg_values_supported: [KnownJwaSignatureAlgorithms.ES256] },
    },
    credential_metadata: {
      display: [{ name: 'Identity card', locale: 'en', background_color: '#1d3557', text_color: '#ffffff' }],
      claims: [
```
