```ts
        { path: ['given_name'], display: [{ name: 'Given name', locale: 'en' }] },
        { path: ['family_name'], display: [{ name: 'Family name', locale: 'en' }] },
        { path: ['birthdate'], display: [{ name: 'Date of birth', locale: 'en' }] },
        { path: ['address', 'country'], display: [{ name: 'Country', locale: 'en' }] },
      ],
    },
  },
} satisfies Record<string, OpenId4VciCredentialConfigurationSupportedWithFormats>

// The issuer certificate is created once the issuer agent is initialized (see below)
let issuerCertificate: X509Certificate

const credentialRequestToCredentialMapper: OpenId4VciCredentialRequestToCredentialMapper = async ({
  credentialConfiguration,
  holderBinding,
  issuanceSession,
}) => {
  if (credentialConfiguration.format !== OpenId4VciCredentialFormatProfile.SdJwtDc) {
    throw new Error(`Unsupported credential format ${credentialConfiguration.format}`)
  }
  if (holderBinding.bindingMethod !== 'jwk') throw new Error('Only jwk holder binding is supported')

  // Look up the data for this user, e.g. based on the issuance metadata of the offer
  const { userId } = issuanceSession.issuanceMetadata ?? {}
  if (userId !== 'user-123') throw new Error('Unknown user')

  return {
    type: 'credentials',
    format: ClaimFormat.SdJwtDc,
    // One credential per holder key (more than one with batch issuance)
    credentials: holderBinding.keys.map((holder) => ({
      holder,
      issuer: { method: 'x5c', x5c: [issuerCertificate], issuer: issuerUrl },
      payload: {
        vct: credentialConfiguration.vct,
        given_name: 'Erika',
        family_name: 'Mustermann',
        birthdate: '1984-01-26',
        address: { street_address: 'Heidestraße 17', locality: 'Köln', country: 'DE' },
      },
      disclosureFrame: {
        _sd: ['given_name', 'family_name', 'birthdate'],
        address: { _sd: ['street_address', 'locality', 'country'] },
      },
    })),
  } satisfies OpenId4VciSignSdJwtCredentials
}

const issuerApp = express()
const issuer = new Agent({
  config: { allowInsecureHttpUrls: true },
  dependencies: agentDependencies,
  modules: {
    ...issuerStorage,
    openid4vc: new OpenId4VcModule({
      app: issuerApp,
      issuer: { baseUrl: `${issuerUrl}/oid4vci`, credentialRequestToCredentialMapper },
    }),
  },
})

const verifierApp = express()
const verifier = new Agent({
  config: { allowInsecureHttpUrls: true },
  dependencies: agentDependencies,
  modules: {
    ...verifierStorage,
    openid4vc: new OpenId4VcModule({ app: verifierApp, verifier: { baseUrl: `${verifierUrl}/oid4vp` } }),
  },
})

const holder = new Agent({
  config: { allowInsecureHttpUrls: true },
  dependencies: agentDependencies,
  modules: {
    ...holderStorage,
    openid4vc: new OpenId4VcModule(),
  },
})

await issuer.initialize()
await verifier.initialize()
await holder.initialize()
const issuerServer = issuerApp.listen(4031)
const verifierServer = verifierApp.listen(4032)

// Self-signed certificate for the example. The SAN must match the host of `issuerUrl`.
issuerCertificate = await issuer.x509.createCertificate({
  authorityKey: PublicJwk.fromPublicJwk((await issuer.kms.createKey({ type: { kty: 'EC', crv: 'P-256' } })).publicJwk),
  issuer: { commonName: 'Credo example issuer', countryName: 'NL' },
  extensions: { subjectAlternativeName: { name: [{ type: 'dns', value: 'localhost' }] } },
})

// Both the holder and the verifier only accept credentials from issuers they trust
holder.x509.config.addTrustedCertificate(issuerCertificate)
verifier.x509.config.addTrustedCertificate(issuerCertificate)

const issuerRecord = await issuer.openid4vc.issuer.createIssuer({
  issuerId: 'example-issuer',
  display: [{ name: 'Credo example issuer', locale: 'en' }],
  credentialConfigurationsSupported,
})

const { credentialOffer } = await issuer.openid4vc.issuer.createCredentialOffer({
  issuerId: issuerRecord.issuerId,
  credentialConfigurationIds: ['identity-sd-jwt'],
  preAuthorizedCodeFlowConfig: {},
  issuanceMetadata: { userId: 'user-123' },
})

const resolvedOffer = await holder.openid4vc.holder.resolveCredentialOffer(credentialOffer)
const token = await holder.openid4vc.holder.requestToken({ resolvedCredentialOffer: resolvedOffer })

const { credentials } = await holder.openid4vc.holder.requestCredentials({
  resolvedCredentialOffer: resolvedOffer,
  ...token,
  credentialBindingResolver: async ({ proofTypes }) => {
    const algorithm = proofTypes.jwt?.supportedSignatureAlgorithms[0]
    if (!algorithm) throw new Error('No supported proof of possession algorithm')

    const key = await holder.kms.createKeyForSignatureAlgorithm({ algorithm })
    return { method: 'jwk', keys: [PublicJwk.fromPublicJwk(key.publicJwk)] }
  },
})

for (const { record } of credentials) {
  if (!(record instanceof SdJwtVcRecord)) throw new Error('Expected an SD-JWT VC')

  await holder.sdJwtVc.store({ record })
  console.log('Stored SD-JWT VC with claims', record.firstCredential.prettyClaims)
}

const verifierRecord = await verifier.openid4vc.verifier.createVerifier({
  verifierId: 'example-verifier',
  clientMetadata: { client_name: 'Credo example verifier' },
})

const { authorizationRequest, verificationSession } = await verifier.openid4vc.verifier.createAuthorizationRequest({
  verifierId: verifierRecord.verifierId,
  requestSigner: { method: 'none' },
  dcql: {
    query: {
      credentials: [
        {
          id: 'identity',
          format: 'dc+sd-jwt',
          meta: { vct_values: ['urn:example:identity:1'] },
          // Only these claims are disclosed, the others stay hidden
          claims: [{ path: ['given_name'] }, { path: ['address', 'country'] }],
        },
      ],
    },
  },
  transactionData: [
    {
      type: 'urn:example:transaction:age-check',
      credential_ids: ['identity'],
      transaction_data_hashes_alg: ['sha-256'],
    },
  ],
})

const resolvedRequest = await holder.openid4vc.holder.resolveOpenId4VpAuthorizationRequest(authorizationRequest)
if (!resolvedRequest.dcql?.queryResult.can_be_satisfied) throw new Error('No matching credentials')

const result = await holder.openid4vc.holder.acceptOpenId4VpAuthorizationRequest({
  authorizationRequestPayload: resolvedRequest.authorizationRequestPayload,
  dcql: { credentials: holder.openid4vc.holder.selectCredentialsForDcqlRequest(resolvedRequest.dcql.queryResult) },
  // Sign each transaction data entry with one of the credentials it lists
  transactionData: resolvedRequest.transactionData?.map(({ matchedCredentialIds }) => ({
    credentialId: matchedCredentialIds[0],
  })),
})
if (!result.ok) throw new Error(`Verifier rejected the presentation: ${result.serverResponse.status}`)

const { dcql, transactionData } = await verifier.openid4vc.verifier.getVerifiedAuthorizationResponse(
  verificationSession.id
)

const [presentation] = dcql?.presentations.identity ?? []
if (presentation?.claimFormat !== ClaimFormat.SdJwtDc) throw new Error('Expected an SD-JWT VC presentation')

// Only the disclosed claims (plus the always visible ones, like vct and iss)
console.log('Disclosed claims', presentation.prettyClaims)
console.log(
  'Signed transaction data',
  transactionData?.map(({ decoded }) => decoded.type)
)

issuerServer.close()
verifierServer.close()
await issuer.shutdown()
await verifier.shutdown()
await holder.shutdown()
```

</details>

## Next steps

- [SD-JWT VC](https://credo.js.org/guides/credential-formats/sd-jwt-vc.md): signing, presenting and verifying outside OpenID4VC.
- [Digital Credentials API](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/dc-api.md): request SD-JWT VCs from a website.
- [Authorization and wallet security](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/authorization.md): DPoP, wallet attestations and key attestations.

# mdoc with OpenID4VC

> Issue, receive and verify ISO 18013-5 mdocs, such as mobile driving licences, over OpenID4VCI and OpenID4VP with Credo.

This page covers what is specific to mdoc (ISO/IEC 18013-5, `mso_mdoc`) in OpenID4VC, in the order of the flow. Issuance covers the issuer's credential configuration, certificate and signing, and the holder's trust and storage. Presentation covers the verifier's DCQL query and the result. [Issuing credentials](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/issuer.md), [Receiving credentials](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/receive.md), [Presenting credentials](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/present.md) and [Verifying credentials](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/verifier.md) explain the flow itself, and [mdoc](https://credo.js.org/guides/credential-formats/mdoc.md) explains the format.

Use mdoc for credentials that follow an ISO document type, such as the mobile driving licence, or that holders also present in person ([ISO mdoc](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/mdoc.md)). To request mdocs from a website, see [Digital Credentials API](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/dc-api.md).

## Issuance

### Configure the credential

Add an `mso_mdoc` entry to the `credentialConfigurationsSupported` of the issuer:

:::issuer

```ts
const mdlNamespace = 'org.iso.18013.5.1'

const credentialConfigurationsSupported = {
  'mdl-mdoc': {
    format: OpenId4VciCredentialFormatProfile.MsoMdoc,
    doctype: 'org.iso.18013.5.1.mDL',
    scope: 'mdl',
    cryptographic_binding_methods_supported: ['cose_key'],
    proof_types_supported: {
      jwt: { proof_signing_alg_values_supported: [KnownJwaSignatureAlgorithms.ES256] },
    },
    credential_metadata: {
      display: [{ name: 'Mobile driving licence', locale: 'en' }],
      claims: [
        { path: [mdlNamespace, 'given_name'], display: [{ name: 'Given name', locale: 'en' }] },
        { path: [mdlNamespace, 'family_name'], display: [{ name: 'Family name', locale: 'en' }] },
        { path: [mdlNamespace, 'birth_date'], display: [{ name: 'Date of birth', locale: 'en' }] },
      ],
    },
  },
} satisfies Record<string, OpenId4VciCredentialConfigurationSupportedWithFormats>
```

:::

- `doctype` is the document type, such as `org.iso.18013.5.1.mDL` for a mobile driving licence. Credo checks that every mdoc the mapper returns has this doctype.
- An mdoc is always bound to a key of the holder, never to a DID. `cose_key` (or `jwk`) in `cryptographic_binding_methods_supported` tells the wallet so.

In `credential_metadata.claims`, the `path` of a data element is its namespace and element identifier. Add a `scope` if you offer the credential through the [authorization code flow](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/authorization.md).

### Create the issuer certificate

mdocs are signed with an X.509 certificate, the document signer certificate:

:::issuer

```ts
// Self-signed for the example. In production this is a document signer certificate issued by your IACA.
issuerCertificate = await issuer.x509.createCertificate({
  authorityKey: PublicJwk.fromPublicJwk((await issuer.kms.createKey({ type: { kty: 'EC', crv: 'P-256' } })).publicJwk),
  // mdoc verification requires a country (C) in the issuer certificate
  issuer: { commonName: 'Credo example mDL issuer', countryName: 'NL' },
})
```

:::

The subject must have a country (`countryName`): verification fails without it, and checks that `issuing_country` in the mdoc matches it (and `issuing_jurisdiction` the state, if present). In production, your issuing authority CA (IACA) issues the document signer certificate, and verifiers trust the IACA certificate. Pass the chain as an array, leaf first, to include it in the mdoc. [X.509 certificates](https://credo.js.org/guides/dids-and-trust/x509.md) explains creating certificates and chains.

### Sign the credential

The mapper returns the mdoc sign options, one entry for each holder key:

:::issuer

```ts
const credentialRequestToCredentialMapper: OpenId4VciCredentialRequestToCredentialMapper = async ({
  credentialConfiguration,
  holderBinding,
}) => {
  if (credentialConfiguration.format !== OpenId4VciCredentialFormatProfile.MsoMdoc) {
    throw new Error(`Unsupported credential format ${credentialConfiguration.format}`)
  }
  // An mdoc is always bound to a key, never to a DID
  if (holderBinding.bindingMethod !== 'jwk') throw new Error('Expected jwk holder binding')

  const oneYearFromNow = new Date(Date.now() + 365 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000)

  return {
    type: 'credentials',
    format: ClaimFormat.MsoMdoc,
    credentials: holderBinding.keys.map(({ jwk }) => ({
      docType: credentialConfiguration.doctype,
      holderKey: jwk,
      issuerCertificate,
      // `signed` and `validFrom` default to now
      validityInfo: { validUntil: oneYearFromNow },
      namespaces: {
        [mdlNamespace]: {
          given_name: 'Erika',
          family_name: 'Mustermann',
          birth_date: new DateOnly('1984-01-26'),
          issue_date: new DateOnly(),
          expiry_date: new DateOnly(oneYearFromNow.toISOString().slice(0, 10)),
          // Must match the country (C) of the issuer certificate
          issuing_country: 'NL',
          document_number: 'NL-123456',
        },
      },
    })),
  } satisfies OpenId4VciSignMdocCredentials
}
```

:::

- `docType` must be the `doctype` of the configuration, and `holderKey` is the key from `holderBinding`.
- `validityInfo` needs `validUntil`. Leave `signed` and `validFrom` out so they default to now: Credo rejects a `validFrom` that is even a few milliseconds before `signed`, which happens if you pass `new Date()`.
- `namespaces` maps each namespace to its data elements. Use `DateOnly` for elements of type `full-date`, such as `birth_date`. Every data element can be disclosed on its own.

For revocation, add `statusInfo` with a [status list](https://credo.js.org/guides/credential-formats/status-lists.md). `keyAuthorizations` lists data elements the wallet may sign itself (device signed).

### Trust the issuer

The holder verifies the mdoc when it receives it, and the verifier verifies it again in the presentation. Both need the issuer certificate or its IACA root:

```ts
// The holder verifies the mdoc when receiving it, and the verifier when it is presented
holder.x509.config.addTrustedCertificate(issuerCertificate)
verifier.x509.config.addTrustedCertificate(issuerCertificate)
```

Without a trusted certificate, verification fails. To decide per verification, for example from a list of IACAs, use `getTrustedIssuersForVerification` in the agent config. See [Trusted issuers](https://credo.js.org/guides/dids-and-trust/trust.md).

### Receive and store

The binding resolver must return keys (`method: 'jwk'`):

:::holder

```ts
const resolvedOffer = await holder.openid4vc.holder.resolveCredentialOffer(credentialOffer)
const token = await holder.openid4vc.holder.requestToken({ resolvedCredentialOffer: resolvedOffer })

const { credentials } = await holder.openid4vc.holder.requestCredentials({
  resolvedCredentialOffer: resolvedOffer,
  ...token,
  // mdoc only supports binding to a key (jwk)
  credentialBindingResolver: async ({ proofTypes }) => {
    const algorithm = proofTypes.jwt?.supportedSignatureAlgorithms[0]
    if (!algorithm) throw new Error('No supported proof of possession algorithm')

    const key = await holder.kms.createKeyForSignatureAlgorithm({ algorithm })
    return { method: 'jwk', keys: [PublicJwk.fromPublicJwk(key.publicJwk)] }
  },
})

for (const { record } of credentials) {
  if (!(record instanceof MdocRecord)) throw new Error('Expected an mdoc')

  await holder.mdoc.store({ record })
  console.log(record.firstCredential.docType, record.firstCredential.issuerSignedNamespaces)
}
```

:::

`requestCredentials` doesn't store anything. The `MdocRecord` has one instance per mdoc the issuer returned. `record.firstCredential.issuerSignedNamespaces` has the data elements per namespace.

## Presentation

The verifier needs the same trust configuration as the holder, see [Trust the issuer](#trust-the-issuer).

### Request data elements with DCQL

The verifier asks for an mdoc by doctype and lists the data elements it needs:

:::verifier

```ts
const { authorizationRequest, verificationSession } = await verifier.openid4vc.verifier.createAuthorizationRequest({
  verifierId: verifierRecord.verifierId,
  requestSigner: { method: 'none' },
  // Encrypted response (the default)
  responseMode: 'direct_post.jwt',
  dcql: {
    query: {
      credentials: [
        {
          id: 'mdl',
          format: 'mso_mdoc',
          meta: { doctype_value: 'org.iso.18013.5.1.mDL' },
          claims: [
            { path: ['org.iso.18013.5.1', 'given_name'], intent_to_retain: false },
            { path: ['org.iso.18013.5.1', 'birth_date'], intent_to_retain: false },
          ],
        },
      ],
    },
  },
})
```

:::

`format` is `mso_mdoc` and `meta.doctype_value` the doctype. Each claim `path` is a namespace and a data element identifier, and `intent_to_retain` tells the wallet whether you store the element. The wallet discloses only the requested data elements. Keep the default response mode `direct_post.jwt`: with OpenID4VP drafts 21 and 24, mdoc requests require it.

### Present

Presenting works as for other formats. Credo creates an ISO 18013-5 device response, signed with the key the mdoc is bound to:

:::holder

```ts
const resolvedRequest = await holder.openid4vc.holder.resolveOpenId4VpAuthorizationRequest(authorizationRequest)
if (!resolvedRequest.dcql?.queryResult.can_be_satisfied) throw new Error('No matching mdoc')

const result = await holder.openid4vc.holder.acceptOpenId4VpAuthorizationRequest({
  authorizationRequestPayload: resolvedRequest.authorizationRequestPayload,
  dcql: { credentials: holder.openid4vc.holder.selectCredentialsForDcqlRequest(resolvedRequest.dcql.queryResult) },
})
if (!result.ok) throw new Error(`Verifier rejected the presentation: ${result.serverResponse.status}`)
```

:::

### Read the disclosed data elements

After the session reaches `ResponseVerified`, the presentation is an `MdocDeviceResponse`:

:::verifier

```ts
const { dcql } = await verifier.openid4vc.verifier.getVerifiedAuthorizationResponse(verificationSession.id)

const [deviceResponse] = dcql?.presentations.mdl ?? []
if (deviceResponse?.claimFormat !== ClaimFormat.MsoMdoc) throw new Error('Expected an mdoc presentation')

// { 'org.iso.18013.5.1.mDL': { 'org.iso.18013.5.1': { given_name: 'Erika', birth_date: DateOnly } } }
console.log(deviceResponse.issuerClaims)
```

:::

`issuerClaims` has the issuer-signed data elements per doctype and namespace. `deviceClaims` has the data elements the wallet signed itself, if any.

## Full example

The issuer, holder and verifier from this page in one process:

<details>
<summary>openid4vc-mdoc.ts</summary>

```ts
import { Agent, ClaimFormat, DateOnly, MdocRecord, type X509Certificate } from '@credo-ts/core'
import { KnownJwaSignatureAlgorithms, PublicJwk } from '@credo-ts/core/kms'
import { openid4vcBundle } from '@credo-ts/drizzle-storage/openid4vc'
import { agentDependencies } from '@credo-ts/node'
import {
  type OpenId4VciCredentialConfigurationSupportedWithFormats,
  OpenId4VciCredentialFormatProfile,
  type OpenId4VciCredentialRequestToCredentialMapper,
  type OpenId4VciSignMdocCredentials,
  OpenId4VcModule,
} from '@credo-ts/openid4vc'
import express from 'express'
import { exampleStorage } from './example-storage.js'

const issuerUrl = 'http://localhost:4033'
const verifierUrl = 'http://localhost:4034'

// In-memory storage and keys, so the example leaves nothing behind
const issuerStorage = await exampleStorage([openid4vcBundle])
const holderStorage = await exampleStorage([openid4vcBundle])

const verifierStorage = await exampleStorage([openid4vcBundle])

const mdlNamespace = 'org.iso.18013.5.1'

const credentialConfigurationsSupported = {
  'mdl-mdoc': {
    format: OpenId4VciCredentialFormatProfile.MsoMdoc,
    doctype: 'org.iso.18013.5.1.mDL',
    scope: 'mdl',
    cryptographic_binding_methods_supported: ['cose_key'],
    proof_types_supported: {
      jwt: { proof_signing_alg_values_supported: [KnownJwaSignatureAlgorithms.ES256] },
    },
    credential_metadata: {
      display: [{ name: 'Mobile driving licence', locale: 'en' }],
      claims: [
        { path: [mdlNamespace, 'given_name'], display: [{ name: 'Given name', locale: 'en' }] },
        { path: [mdlNamespace, 'family_name'], display: [{ name: 'Family name', locale: 'en' }] },
        { path: [mdlNamespace, 'birth_date'], display: [{ name: 'Date of birth', locale: 'en' }] },
      ],
    },
  },
} satisfies Record<string, OpenId4VciCredentialConfigurationSupportedWithFormats>

// The issuer certificate is created once the issuer agent is initialized (see below)
let issuerCertificate: X509Certificate

const credentialRequestToCredentialMapper: OpenId4VciCredentialRequestToCredentialMapper = async ({
  credentialConfiguration,
  holderBinding,
}) => {
  if (credentialConfiguration.format !== OpenId4VciCredentialFormatProfile.MsoMdoc) {
    throw new Error(`Unsupported credential format ${credentialConfiguration.format}`)
  }
  // An mdoc is always bound to a key, never to a DID
  if (holderBinding.bindingMethod !== 'jwk') throw new Error('Expected jwk holder binding')

  const oneYearFromNow = new Date(Date.now() + 365 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000)

  return {
    type: 'credentials',
    format: ClaimFormat.MsoMdoc,
    credentials: holderBinding.keys.map(({ jwk }) => ({
      docType: credentialConfiguration.doctype,
      holderKey: jwk,
      issuerCertificate,
      // `signed` and `validFrom` default to now
      validityInfo: { validUntil: oneYearFromNow },
      namespaces: {
        [mdlNamespace]: {
          given_name: 'Erika',
          family_name: 'Mustermann',
          birth_date: new DateOnly('1984-01-26'),
          issue_date: new DateOnly(),
          expiry_date: new DateOnly(oneYearFromNow.toISOString().slice(0, 10)),
          // Must match the country (C) of the issuer certificate
          issuing_country: 'NL',
          document_number: 'NL-123456',
        },
      },
    })),
  } satisfies OpenId4VciSignMdocCredentials
}

const issuerApp = express()
const issuer = new Agent({
  config: { allowInsecureHttpUrls: true },
  dependencies: agentDependencies,
  modules: {
    ...issuerStorage,
    openid4vc: new OpenId4VcModule({
      app: issuerApp,
      issuer: { baseUrl: `${issuerUrl}/oid4vci`, credentialRequestToCredentialMapper },
    }),
  },
})

const verifierApp = express()
const verifier = new Agent({
  config: { allowInsecureHttpUrls: true },
  dependencies: agentDependencies,
  modules: {
    ...verifierStorage,
    openid4vc: new OpenId4VcModule({ app: verifierApp, verifier: { baseUrl: `${verifierUrl}/oid4vp` } }),
  },
})

const holder = new Agent({
  config: { allowInsecureHttpUrls: true },
  dependencies: agentDependencies,
  modules: {
    ...holderStorage,
    openid4vc: new OpenId4VcModule(),
  },
})

await issuer.initialize()
await verifier.initialize()
await holder.initialize()
const issuerServer = issuerApp.listen(4033)
const verifierServer = verifierApp.listen(4034)

// Self-signed for the example. In production this is a document signer certificate issued by your IACA.
issuerCertificate = await issuer.x509.createCertificate({
  authorityKey: PublicJwk.fromPublicJwk((await issuer.kms.createKey({ type: { kty: 'EC', crv: 'P-256' } })).publicJwk),
  // mdoc verification requires a country (C) in the issuer certificate
  issuer: { commonName: 'Credo example mDL issuer', countryName: 'NL' },
})

// The holder verifies the mdoc when receiving it, and the verifier when it is presented
holder.x509.config.addTrustedCertificate(issuerCertificate)
verifier.x509.config.addTrustedCertificate(issuerCertificate)

const issuerRecord = await issuer.openid4vc.issuer.createIssuer({
  issuerId: 'example-mdl-issuer',
  credentialConfigurationsSupported,
})

const { credentialOffer } = await issuer.openid4vc.issuer.createCredentialOffer({
  issuerId: issuerRecord.issuerId,
  credentialConfigurationIds: ['mdl-mdoc'],
  preAuthorizedCodeFlowConfig: {},
})

const resolvedOffer = await holder.openid4vc.holder.resolveCredentialOffer(credentialOffer)
const token = await holder.openid4vc.holder.requestToken({ resolvedCredentialOffer: resolvedOffer })

const { credentials } = await holder.openid4vc.holder.requestCredentials({
  resolvedCredentialOffer: resolvedOffer,
  ...token,
  // mdoc only supports binding to a key (jwk)
  credentialBindingResolver: async ({ proofTypes }) => {
    const algorithm = proofTypes.jwt?.supportedSignatureAlgorithms[0]
    if (!algorithm) throw new Error('No supported proof of possession algorithm')

    const key = await holder.kms.createKeyForSignatureAlgorithm({ algorithm })
    return { method: 'jwk', keys: [PublicJwk.fromPublicJwk(key.publicJwk)] }
  },
})

for (const { record } of credentials) {
  if (!(record instanceof MdocRecord)) throw new Error('Expected an mdoc')

  await holder.mdoc.store({ record })
  console.log(record.firstCredential.docType, record.firstCredential.issuerSignedNamespaces)
}

const verifierRecord = await verifier.openid4vc.verifier.createVerifier({ verifierId: 'example-verifier' })

const { authorizationRequest, verificationSession } = await verifier.openid4vc.verifier.createAuthorizationRequest({
  verifierId: verifierRecord.verifierId,
  requestSigner: { method: 'none' },
  // Encrypted response (the default)
  responseMode: 'direct_post.jwt',
  dcql: {
    query: {
      credentials: [
        {
          id: 'mdl',
          format: 'mso_mdoc',
          meta: { doctype_value: 'org.iso.18013.5.1.mDL' },
          claims: [
            { path: ['org.iso.18013.5.1', 'given_name'], intent_to_retain: false },
            { path: ['org.iso.18013.5.1', 'birth_date'], intent_to_retain: false },
          ],
        },
      ],
    },
  },
})

const resolvedRequest = await holder.openid4vc.holder.resolveOpenId4VpAuthorizationRequest(authorizationRequest)
if (!resolvedRequest.dcql?.queryResult.can_be_satisfied) throw new Error('No matching mdoc')

const result = await holder.openid4vc.holder.acceptOpenId4VpAuthorizationRequest({
  authorizationRequestPayload: resolvedRequest.authorizationRequestPayload,
  dcql: { credentials: holder.openid4vc.holder.selectCredentialsForDcqlRequest(resolvedRequest.dcql.queryResult) },
})
if (!result.ok) throw new Error(`Verifier rejected the presentation: ${result.serverResponse.status}`)

const { dcql } = await verifier.openid4vc.verifier.getVerifiedAuthorizationResponse(verificationSession.id)

const [deviceResponse] = dcql?.presentations.mdl ?? []
if (deviceResponse?.claimFormat !== ClaimFormat.MsoMdoc) throw new Error('Expected an mdoc presentation')

// { 'org.iso.18013.5.1.mDL': { 'org.iso.18013.5.1': { given_name: 'Erika', birth_date: DateOnly } } }
console.log(deviceResponse.issuerClaims)

issuerServer.close()
verifierServer.close()
await issuer.shutdown()
await verifier.shutdown()
await holder.shutdown()
```

</details>

## Next steps

- [mdoc](https://credo.js.org/guides/credential-formats/mdoc.md): signing, presenting and verifying outside OpenID4VC.
- [Digital Credentials API](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/dc-api.md): request mdocs from a website, with OpenID4VP or ISO 18013-7 Annex C.
- [ISO mdoc](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/mdoc.md): present mdocs in person.
- [Authorization and wallet security](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/authorization.md): DPoP, wallet attestations and key attestations.

# W3C VCs with OpenID4VC

> Issue, receive and verify W3C Verifiable Credentials over OpenID4VCI and OpenID4VP with Credo, as VCDM 1.1 JWTs or VCDM 2.0 SD-JWTs.

This page covers W3C Verifiable Credentials over OpenID4VC: which forms work, then issuance (the issuer's credential configurations and signing, and DID binding on the holder) and presentation (the verifier's DCQL query and the result). [Issuing credentials](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/issuer.md), [Receiving credentials](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/receive.md), [Presenting credentials](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/present.md) and [Verifying credentials](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/verifier.md) explain the flow itself, and [W3C Verifiable Credentials](https://credo.js.org/guides/credential-formats/w3c-vc.md) explains the formats.

Use W3C VCs only when your ecosystem requires the W3C data model. Otherwise [SD-JWT VC](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/sd-jwt-vc.md) is simpler: it binds to a key instead of a DID and is what HAIP requires.

## Supported forms

| Data model | Secured as | OpenID4VCI `format` | Issue and receive | Present with DCQL |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| VCDM 1.1 | JWT | `jwt_vc_json` | Yes | Yes, `jwt_vc_json` |
| VCDM 2.0 | SD-JWT | `vc+sd-jwt` with `credential_definition` | Yes | Yes, `vc+sd-jwt` with `meta.type_values` |
| VCDM 1.1 | JSON-LD (Linked Data Proofs) | `ldp_vc` | Not recommended | No |
| VCDM 2.0 | JWT or Data Integrity | none | No | No |

Use `jwt_vc_json` for VCDM 1.1, or `vc+sd-jwt` for VCDM 2.0 with selective disclosure. The rest of this page uses those two. [Limitations](#limitations) explains the other rows.

## Issuance

### Configure the credentials

:::issuer

```ts
const credentialConfigurationsSupported = {
  // W3C VCDM 1.1, signed as a JWT
  'degree-jwt': {
    format: OpenId4VciCredentialFormatProfile.JwtVcJson,
    credential_definition: { type: ['VerifiableCredential', 'UniversityDegreeCredential'] },
    scope: 'degree-jwt',
    cryptographic_binding_methods_supported: ['did:key'],
    proof_types_supported: {
      jwt: { proof_signing_alg_values_supported: [KnownJwaSignatureAlgorithms.EdDSA] },
    },
  },
  // W3C VCDM 2.0, secured with SD-JWT. No `vct`, otherwise it is an SD-JWT VC.
  'degree-sd-jwt': {
    format: OpenId4VciCredentialFormatProfile.SdJwtVc,
    credential_definition: { type: ['VerifiableCredential', 'UniversityDegreeCredential'] },
    scope: 'degree-sd-jwt',
    cryptographic_binding_methods_supported: ['did:key'],
    proof_types_supported: {
      jwt: { proof_signing_alg_values_supported: [KnownJwaSignatureAlgorithms.EdDSA] },
    },
  },
} satisfies Record<string, OpenId4VciCredentialConfigurationSupportedWithFormats>
```

:::

- `credential_definition.type` lists the credential types. `vc+sd-jwt` with a `credential_definition` and no `vct` is a W3C VCDM 2.0 credential. With a `vct` it's an [SD-JWT VC](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/sd-jwt-vc.md).
- W3C credentials are bound to a DID of the holder, so list DID methods in `cryptographic_binding_methods_supported` (or `did` for any method). Credo doesn't bind W3C credentials to a bare key.

Add a `scope` if you offer the credentials through the [authorization code flow](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/authorization.md).

### Sign the credentials

The issuer signs with a DID that it created in its own agent, and the mapper puts the holder's DID in the credential:

:::issuer

```ts
const credentialRequestToCredentialMapper: OpenId4VciCredentialRequestToCredentialMapper = async ({
  credentialConfiguration,
  holderBinding,
}) => {
  // W3C credentials are bound to a DID of the holder
  if (holderBinding.bindingMethod !== 'did') throw new Error('Expected did holder binding')

  if (credentialConfiguration.format === OpenId4VciCredentialFormatProfile.JwtVcJson) {
    return {
      type: 'credentials',
      format: ClaimFormat.JwtVc,
      credentials: holderBinding.keys.map(({ didUrl }) => ({
        verificationMethod: issuerDid.verificationMethodId,
        credential: new W3cCredential({
          type: credentialConfiguration.credential_definition.type,
          issuer: new W3cIssuer({ id: issuerDid.did }),
          issuanceDate: w3cDate(Date.now()),
          credentialSubject: new W3cCredentialSubject({
            id: parseDid(didUrl).did,
            claims: { degree: 'Bachelor of Science' },
          }),
        }),
      })),
    } satisfies OpenId4VciSignW3cCredentials
  }

  // `vc+sd-jwt` with a `credential_definition` (and no `vct`) is a W3C VCDM 2.0 credential
  if (
    credentialConfiguration.format === OpenId4VciCredentialFormatProfile.SdJwtVc &&
    credentialConfiguration.credential_definition
  ) {
    return {
      type: 'credentials',
      format: ClaimFormat.SdJwtW3cVc,
      credentials: holderBinding.keys.map(({ didUrl }) => ({
        alg: KnownJwaSignatureAlgorithms.EdDSA,
        verificationMethod: issuerDid.verificationMethodId,
        holder: { method: 'did', didUrl },
        credential: new W3cV2Credential({
          type: credentialConfiguration.credential_definition.type,
          issuer: new W3cV2Issuer({ id: issuerDid.did }),
          validFrom: w3cDate(Date.now()),
          credentialSubject: new W3cV2CredentialSubject({ id: parseDid(didUrl).did, degree: 'Bachelor of Science' }),
        }),
        disclosureFrame: { credentialSubject: { _sd: ['degree'] } },
      })),
    } satisfies OpenId4VciSignW3cV2Credentials
  }

  throw new Error(`Unsupported credential configuration ${credentialConfiguration.format}`)
}
```

:::

- `issuerDid` is a DID created with `agent.dids.create`, for example `did:key`, and `verificationMethod` is the id of its signing key. W3C credentials can't be signed with an X.509 certificate. See [DIDs](https://credo.js.org/guides/dids-and-trust.md).
- `holderBinding.keys` has a `didUrl` for each holder key. Its DID becomes the credential subject.
- For VCDM 1.1 (`ClaimFormat.JwtVc`), return a `W3cCredential` and the verification method. Credo picks the JWT algorithm from the key.
- For VCDM 2.0 (`ClaimFormat.SdJwtW3cVc`), return a `W3cV2Credential`, the `alg`, the `holder` (written to `cnf`) and a `disclosureFrame`.

Don't add a `credentialStatus`: Credo can't check it, and a Credo verifier rejects VCDM 1.1 presentations of credentials that have one.

### Receive and store

The holder needs a DID it controls, and the binding resolver returns its verification method:

:::holder

```ts
const holderDid = await createDidKey(holder.dids)

const resolvedOffer = await holder.openid4vc.holder.resolveCredentialOffer(credentialOffer)
const token = await holder.openid4vc.holder.requestToken({ resolvedCredentialOffer: resolvedOffer })

const { credentials } = await holder.openid4vc.holder.requestCredentials({
  resolvedCredentialOffer: resolvedOffer,
  ...token,
  // W3C credentials can only be bound to a DID
  credentialBindingResolver: () => ({ method: 'did', didUrls: [holderDid.verificationMethodId] }),
})

for (const { record } of credentials) {
  if (record instanceof W3cCredentialRecord) await holder.w3cCredentials.store({ record })
  else if (record instanceof W3cV2CredentialRecord) await holder.w3cV2Credentials.store({ record })
  else throw new Error('Expected a W3C credential')
}
```

:::

VCDM 1.1 credentials arrive as a `W3cCredentialRecord`, which you store with `agent.w3cCredentials`. VCDM 2.0 credentials arrive as a `W3cV2CredentialRecord`, stored with `agent.w3cV2Credentials`. Credo verifies both before returning them, and accepts any DID issuer unless you configure [trusted issuers](https://credo.js.org/guides/dids-and-trust/trust.md).

## Presentation

### Request with DCQL

:::verifier

```ts
const { authorizationRequest, verificationSession } = await verifier.openid4vc.verifier.createAuthorizationRequest({
  verifierId: verifierRecord.verifierId,
  requestSigner: { method: 'none' },
  dcql: {
    query: {
      credentials: [
        {
          id: 'degree-jwt',
          format: 'jwt_vc_json',
          meta: { type_values: [['UniversityDegreeCredential']] },
        },
        {
          id: 'degree-sd-jwt',
          format: 'vc+sd-jwt',
          meta: { type_values: [['UniversityDegreeCredential']] },
          claims: [{ path: ['credentialSubject', 'degree'] }],
        },
      ],
    },
  },
})
```

:::

`meta.type_values` lists alternative sets of types. Credo compares them with the `type` values as they appear in the credential, not with expanded JSON-LD IRIs. For `jwt_vc_json`, the wallet presents the whole credential. For `vc+sd-jwt`, the `meta.type_values` make it a W3C VCDM 2.0 query, and `claims` paths point into the credential, for example `['credentialSubject', 'degree']`. The wallet discloses only those claims.

### Present

Presenting works as for other formats. The holder signs the presentation with the DID of the credential subject (VCDM 1.1) or the key in `cnf` (VCDM 2.0):

:::holder

```ts
const resolvedRequest = await holder.openid4vc.holder.resolveOpenId4VpAuthorizationRequest(authorizationRequest)
if (!resolvedRequest.dcql?.queryResult.can_be_satisfied) throw new Error('No matching credentials')

const result = await holder.openid4vc.holder.acceptOpenId4VpAuthorizationRequest({
  authorizationRequestPayload: resolvedRequest.authorizationRequestPayload,
  dcql: { credentials: holder.openid4vc.holder.selectCredentialsForDcqlRequest(resolvedRequest.dcql.queryResult) },
})
if (!result.ok) throw new Error(`Verifier rejected the presentation: ${result.serverResponse.status}`)
```

:::

### Read the presentations

:::verifier

```ts
const { dcql } = await verifier.openid4vc.verifier.getVerifiedAuthorizationResponse(verificationSession.id)

const [jwtPresentation] = dcql?.presentations['degree-jwt'] ?? []
if (jwtPresentation?.claimFormat !== ClaimFormat.JwtVp) throw new Error('Expected a JWT VP')
for (const credential of asArray(jwtPresentation.verifiableCredential)) {
  console.log(credential.type, credential.credentialSubject)
}

const [sdJwtPresentation] = dcql?.presentations['degree-sd-jwt'] ?? []
if (sdJwtPresentation?.claimFormat !== ClaimFormat.SdJwtW3cVp) throw new Error('Expected an SD-JWT VP')
for (const entry of asArray(sdJwtPresentation.resolvedPresentation.verifiableCredential)) {
  // The SD-JWT credential is enveloped in the presentation, with only the disclosed claims
  if ('resolvedCredential' in entry)
    console.log(entry.resolvedCredential.type, entry.resolvedCredential.credentialSubject)
}
```

:::

A `jwt_vc_json` query gives a `W3cJwtVerifiablePresentation`, with the credentials in `verifiableCredential`. A `vc+sd-jwt` query gives a `W3cV2SdJwtVerifiablePresentation`: the credential is enveloped in it, and `resolvedCredential` has the disclosed claims.

## Limitations

- `ldp_vc` (JSON-LD credentials with Linked Data Proofs) has known problems in this version: issuing between Credo agents needs workarounds, and presenting with DCQL fails when Credo creates the presentation.
- `jwt_vc_json-ld` is issued and stored like `jwt_vc_json`, but DCQL has no format for it.
- VCDM 2.0 credentials secured as a plain JWT (`vc+jwt`) or with Data Integrity proofs have no OpenID4VCI format.
- DIF Presentation Exchange only works with the OpenID4VP drafts, and not for VCDM 2.0 credentials.

## Full example

The issuer, holder and verifier from this page in one process:

<details>
<summary>openid4vc-w3c.ts</summary>

```ts
import {
  Agent,
  asArray,
  ClaimFormat,
  type DidsApi,
  type KeyDidCreateOptions,
  parseDid,
  W3cCredential,
  W3cCredentialRecord,
  W3cCredentialSubject,
  W3cIssuer,
  W3cV2Credential,
  W3cV2CredentialRecord,
  W3cV2CredentialSubject,
  W3cV2Issuer,
  w3cDate,
} from '@credo-ts/core'
import { KnownJwaSignatureAlgorithms } from '@credo-ts/core/kms'
import { openid4vcBundle } from '@credo-ts/drizzle-storage/openid4vc'
import { agentDependencies } from '@credo-ts/node'
import {
  type OpenId4VciCredentialConfigurationSupportedWithFormats,
  OpenId4VciCredentialFormatProfile,
  type OpenId4VciCredentialRequestToCredentialMapper,
  type OpenId4VciSignW3cCredentials,
  type OpenId4VciSignW3cV2Credentials,
  OpenId4VcModule,
} from '@credo-ts/openid4vc'
import express from 'express'
import { exampleStorage } from './example-storage.js'

const issuerUrl = 'http://localhost:4035'
const verifierUrl = 'http://localhost:4036'

// In-memory storage and keys, so the example leaves nothing behind
const issuerStorage = await exampleStorage([openid4vcBundle])
const verifierStorage = await exampleStorage([openid4vcBundle])
const holderStorage = await exampleStorage([openid4vcBundle])

async function createDidKey(dids: DidsApi) {
  const { didState } = await dids.create<KeyDidCreateOptions>({
    method: 'key',
    options: { createKey: { type: { kty: 'OKP', crv: 'Ed25519' } } },
  })
  const verificationMethod = didState.didDocument?.verificationMethod?.[0]
  if (didState.state !== 'finished' || !verificationMethod) throw new Error('Failed to create did:key')

  return { did: didState.did, verificationMethodId: verificationMethod.id }
}

const credentialConfigurationsSupported = {
  // W3C VCDM 1.1, signed as a JWT
  'degree-jwt': {
    format: OpenId4VciCredentialFormatProfile.JwtVcJson,
    credential_definition: { type: ['VerifiableCredential', 'UniversityDegreeCredential'] },
    scope: 'degree-jwt',
    cryptographic_binding_methods_supported: ['did:key'],
    proof_types_supported: {
      jwt: { proof_signing_alg_values_supported: [KnownJwaSignatureAlgorithms.EdDSA] },
    },
  },
  // W3C VCDM 2.0, secured with SD-JWT. No `vct`, otherwise it is an SD-JWT VC.
  'degree-sd-jwt': {
    format: OpenId4VciCredentialFormatProfile.SdJwtVc,
    credential_definition: { type: ['VerifiableCredential', 'UniversityDegreeCredential'] },
    scope: 'degree-sd-jwt',
    cryptographic_binding_methods_supported: ['did:key'],
    proof_types_supported: {
      jwt: { proof_signing_alg_values_supported: [KnownJwaSignatureAlgorithms.EdDSA] },
    },
  },
} satisfies Record<string, OpenId4VciCredentialConfigurationSupportedWithFormats>

// The issuer DID is created once the issuer agent is initialized (see below)
let issuerDid: { did: string; verificationMethodId: string }

const credentialRequestToCredentialMapper: OpenId4VciCredentialRequestToCredentialMapper = async ({
  credentialConfiguration,
  holderBinding,
}) => {
  // W3C credentials are bound to a DID of the holder
  if (holderBinding.bindingMethod !== 'did') throw new Error('Expected did holder binding')

  if (credentialConfiguration.format === OpenId4VciCredentialFormatProfile.JwtVcJson) {
    return {
      type: 'credentials',
      format: ClaimFormat.JwtVc,
      credentials: holderBinding.keys.map(({ didUrl }) => ({
        verificationMethod: issuerDid.verificationMethodId,
        credential: new W3cCredential({
          type: credentialConfiguration.credential_definition.type,
          issuer: new W3cIssuer({ id: issuerDid.did }),
          issuanceDate: w3cDate(Date.now()),
          credentialSubject: new W3cCredentialSubject({
            id: parseDid(didUrl).did,
            claims: { degree: 'Bachelor of Science' },
          }),
        }),
      })),
    } satisfies OpenId4VciSignW3cCredentials
  }

  // `vc+sd-jwt` with a `credential_definition` (and no `vct`) is a W3C VCDM 2.0 credential
  if (
    credentialConfiguration.format === OpenId4VciCredentialFormatProfile.SdJwtVc &&
    credentialConfiguration.credential_definition
  ) {
    return {
      type: 'credentials',
      format: ClaimFormat.SdJwtW3cVc,
      credentials: holderBinding.keys.map(({ didUrl }) => ({
        alg: KnownJwaSignatureAlgorithms.EdDSA,
        verificationMethod: issuerDid.verificationMethodId,
        holder: { method: 'did', didUrl },
        credential: new W3cV2Credential({
          type: credentialConfiguration.credential_definition.type,
          issuer: new W3cV2Issuer({ id: issuerDid.did }),
          validFrom: w3cDate(Date.now()),
          credentialSubject: new W3cV2CredentialSubject({ id: parseDid(didUrl).did, degree: 'Bachelor of Science' }),
        }),
        disclosureFrame: { credentialSubject: { _sd: ['degree'] } },
      })),
    } satisfies OpenId4VciSignW3cV2Credentials
  }

  throw new Error(`Unsupported credential configuration ${credentialConfiguration.format}`)
}

const issuerApp = express()
const issuer = new Agent({
  config: { allowInsecureHttpUrls: true },
  dependencies: agentDependencies,
  modules: {
    ...issuerStorage,
    openid4vc: new OpenId4VcModule({
      app: issuerApp,
      issuer: { baseUrl: `${issuerUrl}/oid4vci`, credentialRequestToCredentialMapper },
    }),
  },
})

const verifierApp = express()
const verifier = new Agent({
  config: { allowInsecureHttpUrls: true },
  dependencies: agentDependencies,
  modules: {
    ...verifierStorage,
    openid4vc: new OpenId4VcModule({ app: verifierApp, verifier: { baseUrl: `${verifierUrl}/oid4vp` } }),
  },
})

const holder = new Agent({
  config: { allowInsecureHttpUrls: true },
  dependencies: agentDependencies,
  modules: {
    ...holderStorage,
    openid4vc: new OpenId4VcModule(),
  },
})

await issuer.initialize()
await verifier.initialize()
await holder.initialize()
const issuerServer = issuerApp.listen(4035)
const verifierServer = verifierApp.listen(4036)

issuerDid = await createDidKey(issuer.dids)

const issuerRecord = await issuer.openid4vc.issuer.createIssuer({
  issuerId: 'example-w3c-issuer',
  credentialConfigurationsSupported,
})

const { credentialOffer } = await issuer.openid4vc.issuer.createCredentialOffer({
  issuerId: issuerRecord.issuerId,
  credentialConfigurationIds: ['degree-jwt', 'degree-sd-jwt'],
  preAuthorizedCodeFlowConfig: {},
})

const holderDid = await createDidKey(holder.dids)

const resolvedOffer = await holder.openid4vc.holder.resolveCredentialOffer(credentialOffer)
const token = await holder.openid4vc.holder.requestToken({ resolvedCredentialOffer: resolvedOffer })

const { credentials } = await holder.openid4vc.holder.requestCredentials({
  resolvedCredentialOffer: resolvedOffer,
  ...token,
  // W3C credentials can only be bound to a DID
  credentialBindingResolver: () => ({ method: 'did', didUrls: [holderDid.verificationMethodId] }),
})

for (const { record } of credentials) {
  if (record instanceof W3cCredentialRecord) await holder.w3cCredentials.store({ record })
  else if (record instanceof W3cV2CredentialRecord) await holder.w3cV2Credentials.store({ record })
  else throw new Error('Expected a W3C credential')
}

const verifierRecord = await verifier.openid4vc.verifier.createVerifier({ verifierId: 'example-verifier' })

const { authorizationRequest, verificationSession } = await verifier.openid4vc.verifier.createAuthorizationRequest({
  verifierId: verifierRecord.verifierId,
  requestSigner: { method: 'none' },
  dcql: {
    query: {
      credentials: [
        {
          id: 'degree-jwt',
          format: 'jwt_vc_json',
          meta: { type_values: [['UniversityDegreeCredential']] },
        },
        {
          id: 'degree-sd-jwt',
          format: 'vc+sd-jwt',
          meta: { type_values: [['UniversityDegreeCredential']] },
          claims: [{ path: ['credentialSubject', 'degree'] }],
        },
      ],
    },
  },
})

const resolvedRequest = await holder.openid4vc.holder.resolveOpenId4VpAuthorizationRequest(authorizationRequest)
if (!resolvedRequest.dcql?.queryResult.can_be_satisfied) throw new Error('No matching credentials')

const result = await holder.openid4vc.holder.acceptOpenId4VpAuthorizationRequest({
  authorizationRequestPayload: resolvedRequest.authorizationRequestPayload,
  dcql: { credentials: holder.openid4vc.holder.selectCredentialsForDcqlRequest(resolvedRequest.dcql.queryResult) },
})
if (!result.ok) throw new Error(`Verifier rejected the presentation: ${result.serverResponse.status}`)

const { dcql } = await verifier.openid4vc.verifier.getVerifiedAuthorizationResponse(verificationSession.id)

const [jwtPresentation] = dcql?.presentations['degree-jwt'] ?? []
if (jwtPresentation?.claimFormat !== ClaimFormat.JwtVp) throw new Error('Expected a JWT VP')
for (const credential of asArray(jwtPresentation.verifiableCredential)) {
  console.log(credential.type, credential.credentialSubject)
}

const [sdJwtPresentation] = dcql?.presentations['degree-sd-jwt'] ?? []
if (sdJwtPresentation?.claimFormat !== ClaimFormat.SdJwtW3cVp) throw new Error('Expected an SD-JWT VP')
for (const entry of asArray(sdJwtPresentation.resolvedPresentation.verifiableCredential)) {
  // The SD-JWT credential is enveloped in the presentation, with only the disclosed claims
  if ('resolvedCredential' in entry)
    console.log(entry.resolvedCredential.type, entry.resolvedCredential.credentialSubject)
}

issuerServer.close()
verifierServer.close()
await issuer.shutdown()
await verifier.shutdown()
await holder.shutdown()
```

</details>

## Next steps

- [W3C Verifiable Credentials](https://credo.js.org/guides/credential-formats/w3c-vc.md): signing, presenting and verifying outside OpenID4VC.
- [W3C VCs with DIDComm](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/didcomm/w3c.md): exchange W3C credentials over DIDComm.
- [DIDs](https://credo.js.org/guides/dids-and-trust.md): create the DIDs for issuers and holders.

# ISO mdoc

> How the ISO/IEC 18013-5 and 18013-7 presentation protocols for mdocs work, how they differ from OpenID4VP, and what Credo does for proximity and the Digital Credentials API.

ISO/IEC 18013-5 defines the mdoc, the credential format of the mobile driving licence (mDL), together with a protocol to present it in person. ISO/IEC TS 18013-7 adds presentation over the internet, and its Annex C defines `org-iso-mdoc` for the W3C Digital Credentials API. These protocols carry only mdocs. This page explains how an mdoc presentation works, how it differs from OpenID4VP, and what Credo does for each. For the format, see [mdoc](https://credo.js.org/guides/credential-formats/mdoc.md). To issue mdocs, or to present them over OpenID4VP, see [mdoc with OpenID4VC](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/mdoc.md).

## How a presentation works

The wallet holds the mdoc, and the verifier is called the mdoc reader. A presentation has these parts:

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| Device engagement | Only in proximity. The wallet shows a QR code, or answers an NFC tap, with an ephemeral key and the transports it supports. The reader answers with its own ephemeral key, and both derive session keys that encrypt the rest of the exchange. |
| Device request | Per document type, the data elements the reader wants and whether it keeps them (intent to retain). The reader can sign each document request with its certificate (reader authentication), so the wallet can show who is asking. |
| Device response | The disclosed data elements as the issuer signed them, and a signature over the session transcript made with the device key the mdoc is bound to. |
| Session transcript | Never sent. Both sides derive it from the session: from the engagement in proximity, from the website's origin and the encryption parameters with the Digital Credentials API. The device signature covers it, so a response is only valid in the session it was made for. |

## Proximity and the Digital Credentials API

Credo supports two ways to present an mdoc with these protocols:

| | [Proximity](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/mdoc/proximity.md) | [Digital Credentials API](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/dc-api.md) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Standard | ISO/IEC 18013-5 | ISO/IEC TS 18013-7 Annex C |
| Use | In person, for example at a counter or a gate | A website, through the browser and the operating system |
| Started by | The reader scanning a QR code, or an NFC tap | The page calling `navigator.credentials.get()` with protocol `org-iso-mdoc` |
| Transport | BLE, NFC or Wi-Fi Aware | The browser and the operating system |
| Encryption | Session keys from the engagement | The response is encrypted to the verifier with HPKE |

The Digital Credentials API also carries OpenID4VP requests. [Digital Credentials API](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/dc-api.md) covers both protocols, with a guide for the verifier and one for the wallet.

Which to use depends on where the presentation happens. In person, use proximity. On a website, use the Digital Credentials API, and pass an OpenID4VP and an `org-iso-mdoc` request in one call, as iOS only accepts `org-iso-mdoc`. Where the browser doesn't support the API, fall back to OpenID4VP with a QR code or a link, see [mdoc with OpenID4VC](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/mdoc.md).

## How it differs from OpenID4VP

OpenID4VP can present the same mdoc, and the device response inside it has the same structure. ISO/IEC TS 18013-7 also describes mdoc presentation over OpenID4VP. Everything around the device response differs:

| | ISO 18013-5 and 18013-7 Annex C | OpenID4VP |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Encoding | CBOR | JSON and JWT |
| Request | A device request with document types and data element identifiers | An authorization request with a DCQL query |
| Credential formats | mdoc | SD-JWT VC, mdoc and W3C VCs |
| Alternatives | Can't be expressed. Several document requests can mean all of them or any one. | DCQL credential sets and claim sets |
| Verifier identity | Reader certificate, optional | Client identifier, usually with a signed request |
| Credo API | `agent.mdoc` and `MdocDeviceResponse` in `@credo-ts/core` | `agent.openid4vc` in `@credo-ts/openid4vc` |

## What Credo does

| Step | Proximity | Digital Credentials API |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Engagement and transport | A native module, such as `expo-mdoc-data-transfer` in a React Native wallet | The browser and the operating system. In the wallet, a native module such as `@animo-id/expo-digital-credentials-api` |
| Encryption | The native module | Credo |
| Create the device request | Not supported | `agent.mdoc.createDcApiVerificationSession` |
| Read the request in the wallet | Decode it with `@owf/mdoc` | `agent.mdoc.resolveDcApiRequest`, which also finds matching mdocs |
| Reader authentication | Not checked | Created and verified |
| Create the device response | `MdocDeviceResponse.createDeviceResponse` | `agent.mdoc.createDcApiResponse` |
| Verify the device response | `MdocDeviceResponse.verify` | `agent.mdoc.verifyDcApiResponse`, which also checks the response against the request |

Credo signs device responses with the device key (device signature). It doesn't support device MAC authentication, so it can't verify a response authenticated with a MAC either.

Neither standard covers issuance. Wallets usually receive mdocs over OpenID4VCI, see [mdoc with OpenID4VC](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc/mdoc.md).

- [Proximity (ISO 18013-5)](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/mdoc/proximity.md): Present mdocs in person over BLE after a QR code or NFC engagement from a React Native wallet with expo-mdoc-data-transfer and Credo, and verify the device response in a reader.

# Proximity (ISO 18013-5)

> Present mdocs in person over BLE after a QR code or NFC engagement from a React Native wallet with expo-mdoc-data-transfer and Credo, and verify the device response in a reader.

In a proximity presentation the wallet and the verifier's reader are in the same place, for example at a counter, and exchange the request and response over Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) after the reader scans a QR code or taps the phone. A native module handles the engagement, the transport and the session encryption. Credo creates the device response in the wallet and verifies it in the reader. This page builds a screen for a React Native wallet that uses [`expo-mdoc-data-transfer`](https://github.com/openwallet-foundation-labs/expo-mdoc-data-transfer), then shows how a reader verifies the response. [ISO mdoc](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/mdoc.md) explains the messages.

[Paradym Wallet](https://github.com/animo/paradym-wallet), an open source wallet built on Credo, presents mdocs in person this way. See its [proximity code](https://github.com/animo/paradym-wallet/blob/main/apps/wallet/src/features/proximity/mdocProximity.ts).

## How it works

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant App as Wallet app
  participant Module as Native module
  participant Reader
  App->>Module: start engagement
  Module-->>App: QR code
  Reader->>Module: scan the QR code or tap, connect over BLE
  Reader->>Module: encrypted device request
  Module-->>App: device request and session transcript
  App->>App: ask for consent, create the device response with Credo
  App->>Module: device response
  Module->>Reader: encrypted device response
  Reader->>Reader: verify the device response
```

The module derives the session keys and the session transcript from the engagement, decrypts the request, and encrypts the response. Your app only handles the decrypted device request and the device response.

Credo doesn't decode device requests, so the wallet decodes them with `@owf/mdoc`, the mdoc library Credo builds on. Credo also doesn't check reader authentication on a proximity request, and only supports device signatures, not device MAC authentication.

## Wallet

### Set up

```bash
npm install expo-mdoc-data-transfer expo-build-properties @owf/mdoc@^0.8.2 react-native-qrcode-svg react-native-svg
```

Add the config plugins to `app.json` and run `npx expo prebuild`:

```json
{
  "expo": {
    "plugins": [
      "expo-mdoc-data-transfer",
      ["expo-build-properties", { "android": { "minSdkVersion": 26 }, "ios": { "useFrameworks": "dynamic" } }]
    ]
  }
}
```

- Use the `@owf/mdoc` version that `@credo-ts/core` depends on, so the app has one copy.
- The config plugin adds the Bluetooth and NFC permissions and the NFC engagement service to the Android manifest. See the [module README](https://github.com/openwallet-foundation-labs/expo-mdoc-data-transfer#readme).
- Dynamic frameworks on iOS change how every pod links. Paradym Wallet keeps some pods static, `askar` and `anoncreds` among them, with the plugin option `ios.buildStatic`.

Bluetooth and NFC don't work in emulators, so test on physical devices. Android also asks the user for the Bluetooth permissions at runtime:

:::holder

```ts
// Android 12 and later need the Bluetooth permissions, earlier versions the location permissions
async function requestBluetoothPermissions() {
  if (Platform.OS !== 'android') return

  const { PERMISSIONS } = PermissionsAndroid
  await PermissionsAndroid.requestMultiple(
    Platform.Version >= 31
      ? [PERMISSIONS.BLUETOOTH_ADVERTISE, PERMISSIONS.BLUETOOTH_CONNECT, PERMISSIONS.BLUETOOTH_SCAN]
      : [PERMISSIONS.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION, PERMISSIONS.ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION]
  )
}
```

:::

The wallet itself is an agent with storage and the stored mdocs, see [Your first agent](https://credo.js.org/guides/getting-started/first-agent.md). The screen below gets it as a prop.

### Engage and receive the request

When the user taps the button, the screen starts the engagement, shows the QR code and waits for the reader's request:

:::holder

```tsx
async function start() {
  await requestBluetoothPermissions()

  const transfer = mdocDataTransfer.instance()
  setQrCode(await transfer.startQrEngagement())
  // Also lets the reader engage with an NFC tap. Android only.
  transfer.enableNfc()

  // Resolves when a reader has scanned the QR code, connected over BLE and sent its request.
  // The module decrypts the request and derives the session transcript.
  const { deviceRequest, sessionTranscript } = await transfer.waitForDeviceRequest()
  setReaderRequest({ documentRequests: decodeDeviceRequest(deviceRequest), sessionTranscript })
}
```

:::

`startQrEngagement()` returns the device engagement to show as a QR code. On iOS, the reader always engages by scanning it. `waitForDeviceRequest()` resolves when a reader has connected and sent its request, and rejects when the transfer fails.

`decodeDeviceRequest` reads the requested data elements from the request:

:::holder

```ts
import {
  type Agent,
  CredentialMultiInstanceUseMode,
  isNonEmptyArray,
  type Mdoc,
  MdocDeviceResponse,
  type MdocDocumentRequest,
  TypedArrayEncoder,
  useInstanceFromCredentialRecord,
} from '@credo-ts/core'
import { DeviceRequest } from '@owf/mdoc'

// The requested data elements per document type, with the reader's intent to retain each one
export function decodeDeviceRequest(deviceRequest: Uint8Array): MdocDocumentRequest[] {
  return DeviceRequest.decode(deviceRequest).docRequests.map(({ itemsRequest }) => ({
    docType: itemsRequest.docType,
    nameSpaces: Object.fromEntries(
      Array.from(itemsRequest.namespaces, ([nameSpace, elements]) => [nameSpace, Object.fromEntries(elements)])
    ),
  }))
}
```

:::

`documentRequests` lists, per document type, the requested data elements and the reader's intent to retain each one. The screen shows them to the user before it shares anything.

### Create and send the device response

When the user agrees, the screen creates the device response and hands it to the module. `shutdown()` ends the session, and `useMdocDataTransferShutdownOnUnmount()` in the full example also does that when the user leaves the screen:

:::holder

```tsx
async function share(request: ReaderRequest) {
  const transfer = mdocDataTransfer.instance()
  // The module encrypts the response with the session keys and sends it
  await transfer.sendDeviceResponse(await createDeviceResponse(agent, request))
  stop()
}

function stop() {
  mdocDataTransfer.instance().shutdown()
  setQrCode(undefined)
  setReaderRequest(undefined)
}
```

:::

The device response itself is plain Credo:

:::holder

```ts
export async function createDeviceResponse(
  agent: Agent,
  options: { documentRequests: MdocDocumentRequest[]; sessionTranscript: Uint8Array }
) {
  const mdocs: Mdoc[] = []
  const documentRequests: MdocDocumentRequest[] = []

  for (const { docType, nameSpaces } of options.documentRequests) {
    const [record] = await agent.mdoc.findAllByQuery({ docType })
    if (!record) continue

    // A new instance for every presentation, if the mdoc was issued in a batch
    const { credentialInstance: mdoc } = await useInstanceFromCredentialRecord({
      agentContext: agent.context,
      credentialRecord: record,
      useMode: CredentialMultiInstanceUseMode.NewOrFirst,
    })

    // Disclose the requested elements the mdoc has. Requesting an element it doesn't have fails.
    const issuerSigned = mdoc.issuerSignedNamespaces
    const disclosed = Object.fromEntries(
      Object.entries(nameSpaces).map(([nameSpace, elements]) => [
        nameSpace,
        Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(elements).filter(([element]) => element in (issuerSigned[nameSpace] ?? {}))),
      ])
    )

    mdocs.push(mdoc)
    documentRequests.push({ docType, nameSpaces: disclosed })
  }

  if (!isNonEmptyArray(mdocs)) throw new Error('No mdoc of the requested document types')

  const deviceResponse = await MdocDeviceResponse.createDeviceResponse(agent.context, {
    mdocs,
    documentRequests,
    sessionTranscriptOptions: { type: 'sessionTranscriptBytes', sessionTranscriptBytes: options.sessionTranscript },
  })

  // The encoded DeviceResponse, for the transport to encrypt and send
  return deviceResponse.deviceResponse.encode()
}
```

:::

- `createDeviceResponse` throws when a requested element isn't in the mdoc, so the function only passes the elements the mdoc has. The reader sees the others as missing.
- `useInstanceFromCredentialRecord` takes a new instance of an mdoc issued in a batch, so readers can't link presentations. When no new instance is left, it reuses the first one.

The session transcript from the module goes in as `sessionTranscriptBytes`, and the device key of the mdoc signs over it. The module encrypts the returned `DeviceResponse` with the session keys.

## Reader

Credo doesn't implement the reader side of the transport, and `expo-mdoc-data-transfer` only covers the wallet. When your reader app has the device response and the session transcript from its own transport, Credo verifies the response:

:::verifier

```ts
export async function verifyDeviceResponse(
  agent: Agent,
  options: { deviceResponse: Uint8Array; sessionTranscript: Uint8Array; trustedCertificates: string[] }
) {
  const deviceResponse = MdocDeviceResponse.fromBase64Url(TypedArrayEncoder.toBase64Url(options.deviceResponse))

  // Throws when the response is invalid. Doesn't use the agent's trust configuration.
  await deviceResponse.verify(agent.context, {
    trustedCertificates: options.trustedCertificates,
    sessionTranscriptOptions: { type: 'sessionTranscriptBytes', sessionTranscriptBytes: options.sessionTranscript },
  })

  return deviceResponse.issuerClaims
}
```

:::

- `verify` doesn't use the agent's trust configuration. Pass the certificates of the issuers you trust, usually the IACA root certificates, as `trustedCertificates`, or every response fails.
- `verify` throws when the response is invalid. It checks the issuer signature and certificate chain, the element digests, the device signature over the session transcript, the validity period and the status. It doesn't check that the response contains what you asked for, so check `issuerClaims` (per document type and namespace) yourself.

## Full example

The wallet screen, and the Credo functions it and the reader use. Render `PresentInPersonScreen` with the wallet's agent.

**mdoc-proximity-wallet.tsx**

```tsx
// A screen of a React Native wallet that presents mdocs to a reader in person. expo-mdoc-data-transfer
// handles the engagement and the transport, Credo the device response (mdoc-proximity.ts).

import type { Agent, MdocDocumentRequest } from '@credo-ts/core'
import { mdocDataTransfer, useMdocDataTransferShutdownOnUnmount } from 'expo-mdoc-data-transfer'
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Button, PermissionsAndroid, Platform, Text, View } from 'react-native'
import QRCode from 'react-native-qrcode-svg'
import { createDeviceResponse, decodeDeviceRequest } from './mdoc-proximity.js'

interface ReaderRequest {
  documentRequests: MdocDocumentRequest[]
  sessionTranscript: Uint8Array
}

export function PresentInPersonScreen({ agent }: { agent: Agent }) {
  const [qrCode, setQrCode] = useState<string>()
  const [readerRequest, setReaderRequest] = useState<ReaderRequest>()

  // Ends the session when the user leaves the screen
  useMdocDataTransferShutdownOnUnmount()

  async function start() {
    await requestBluetoothPermissions()

    const transfer = mdocDataTransfer.instance()
    setQrCode(await transfer.startQrEngagement())
    // Also lets the reader engage with an NFC tap. Android only.
    transfer.enableNfc()

    // Resolves when a reader has scanned the QR code, connected over BLE and sent its request.
    // The module decrypts the request and derives the session transcript.
    const { deviceRequest, sessionTranscript } = await transfer.waitForDeviceRequest()
    setReaderRequest({ documentRequests: decodeDeviceRequest(deviceRequest), sessionTranscript })
  }

  async function share(request: ReaderRequest) {
    const transfer = mdocDataTransfer.instance()
    // The module encrypts the response with the session keys and sends it
    await transfer.sendDeviceResponse(await createDeviceResponse(agent, request))
    stop()
  }

  function stop() {
    mdocDataTransfer.instance().shutdown()
    setQrCode(undefined)
    setReaderRequest(undefined)
  }

  if (readerRequest) {
    return (
      <View style={{ gap: 16, padding: 24 }}>
        <Text>The reader asks for:</Text>
        {readerRequest.documentRequests.map(({ docType, nameSpaces }) => (
          <Text key={docType}>
            {docType}: {Object.values(nameSpaces).flatMap(Object.keys).join(', ')}
          </Text>
        ))}
        <Button title="Share" onPress={() => share(readerRequest)} />
        <Button title="Decline" onPress={stop} />
      </View>
    )
  }

  return (
    <View style={{ alignItems: 'center', gap: 16, padding: 24 }}>
      {qrCode ? <QRCode value={qrCode} size={250} /> : <Button title="Show QR code" onPress={start} />}
    </View>
  )
}

// Android 12 and later need the Bluetooth permissions, earlier versions the location permissions
async function requestBluetoothPermissions() {
  if (Platform.OS !== 'android') return

  const { PERMISSIONS } = PermissionsAndroid
  await PermissionsAndroid.requestMultiple(
    Platform.Version >= 31
      ? [PERMISSIONS.BLUETOOTH_ADVERTISE, PERMISSIONS.BLUETOOTH_CONNECT, PERMISSIONS.BLUETOOTH_SCAN]
      : [PERMISSIONS.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION, PERMISSIONS.ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION]
  )
}
```

**mdoc-proximity.ts**

```ts
import {
  type Agent,
  CredentialMultiInstanceUseMode,
  isNonEmptyArray,
  type Mdoc,
  MdocDeviceResponse,
  type MdocDocumentRequest,
  TypedArrayEncoder,
  useInstanceFromCredentialRecord,
} from '@credo-ts/core'
import { DeviceRequest } from '@owf/mdoc'

// The requested data elements per document type, with the reader's intent to retain each one
export function decodeDeviceRequest(deviceRequest: Uint8Array): MdocDocumentRequest[] {
  return DeviceRequest.decode(deviceRequest).docRequests.map(({ itemsRequest }) => ({
    docType: itemsRequest.docType,
    nameSpaces: Object.fromEntries(
      Array.from(itemsRequest.namespaces, ([nameSpace, elements]) => [nameSpace, Object.fromEntries(elements)])
    ),
  }))
}

export async function createDeviceResponse(
  agent: Agent,
  options: { documentRequests: MdocDocumentRequest[]; sessionTranscript: Uint8Array }
) {
  const mdocs: Mdoc[] = []
  const documentRequests: MdocDocumentRequest[] = []

  for (const { docType, nameSpaces } of options.documentRequests) {
    const [record] = await agent.mdoc.findAllByQuery({ docType })
    if (!record) continue

    // A new instance for every presentation, if the mdoc was issued in a batch
    const { credentialInstance: mdoc } = await useInstanceFromCredentialRecord({
      agentContext: agent.context,
      credentialRecord: record,
      useMode: CredentialMultiInstanceUseMode.NewOrFirst,
    })

    // Disclose the requested elements the mdoc has. Requesting an element it doesn't have fails.
    const issuerSigned = mdoc.issuerSignedNamespaces
    const disclosed = Object.fromEntries(
      Object.entries(nameSpaces).map(([nameSpace, elements]) => [
        nameSpace,
        Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(elements).filter(([element]) => element in (issuerSigned[nameSpace] ?? {}))),
      ])
    )

    mdocs.push(mdoc)
    documentRequests.push({ docType, nameSpaces: disclosed })
  }

  if (!isNonEmptyArray(mdocs)) throw new Error('No mdoc of the requested document types')

  const deviceResponse = await MdocDeviceResponse.createDeviceResponse(agent.context, {
    mdocs,
    documentRequests,
    sessionTranscriptOptions: { type: 'sessionTranscriptBytes', sessionTranscriptBytes: options.sessionTranscript },
  })

  // The encoded DeviceResponse, for the transport to encrypt and send
  return deviceResponse.deviceResponse.encode()
}

export async function verifyDeviceResponse(
  agent: Agent,
  options: { deviceResponse: Uint8Array; sessionTranscript: Uint8Array; trustedCertificates: string[] }
) {
  const deviceResponse = MdocDeviceResponse.fromBase64Url(TypedArrayEncoder.toBase64Url(options.deviceResponse))

  // Throws when the response is invalid. Doesn't use the agent's trust configuration.
  await deviceResponse.verify(agent.context, {
    trustedCertificates: options.trustedCertificates,
    sessionTranscriptOptions: { type: 'sessionTranscriptBytes', sessionTranscriptBytes: options.sessionTranscript },
  })

  return deviceResponse.issuerClaims
}
```

## Next steps

- [Digital Credentials API](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/dc-api.md): request mdocs from a website.
- [mdoc](https://credo.js.org/guides/credential-formats/mdoc.md): signing, storing and verifying mdocs.
- [Trusted issuers](https://credo.js.org/guides/dids-and-trust/trust.md): decide which issuers you trust.

# Digital Credentials API

> How the W3C Digital Credentials API passes credential requests from a website to a wallet, the two protocols Credo supports over it (OpenID4VP and ISO 18013-7 Annex C), platform support, and which protocols and options to choose.

The W3C Digital Credentials API lets a website request credentials through the browser. The browser and the operating system let the user pick a wallet and a credential, on the same device or on a phone nearby, without QR codes or redirects. The API only carries the request and the response, and another protocol defines what they contain. Credo supports two, OpenID4VP and ISO 18013-7 Annex C, on both the verifier and the wallet side.

This page explains how the API works and what to choose. To build one side, see [Building a verifier](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/dc-api/verifier.md) or [Building a wallet](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/dc-api/wallet.md).

## How it works

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant Backend as Verifier backend
  participant Page as Web page
  participant Browser as Browser and OS
  participant Wallet
  Wallet->>Browser: register credentials
  Page->>Backend: create requests
  Backend-->>Page: requests
  Page->>Browser: navigator.credentials.get()
  Browser->>Browser: user picks a wallet and a credential
  Browser->>Wallet: request and origin of the page
  Wallet-->>Browser: response
  Browser-->>Page: response
  Page->>Backend: response
  Backend->>Backend: verify for the origin
```

The wallet registers its credentials with the operating system beforehand, so the browser only offers wallets that hold a matching credential. The verifier's backend creates the request with Credo, and its web page passes it to `navigator.credentials.get()`. The page can pass several requests in one call, one per protocol, and the wallet answers one of them.

The browser tells the wallet the origin of the page that asked. The wallet binds its response to that origin, and the backend verifies the response for its own origin, so a response can't be relayed to another website. Nothing goes over the network between the wallet and the verifier: the response comes back through the page.

## Protocols

| | OpenID4VP | ISO 18013-7 Annex C |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Protocol identifier | `openid4vp-v1-unsigned` or `openid4vp-v1-signed` | `org-iso-mdoc` |
| Credential formats | SD-JWT VC and mdoc | mdoc |
| Request | A DCQL query, which can express alternatives | A device request: document types and data elements |
| Verifier identity | The origin, or a signed request | The origin, or reader authentication |
| Response encryption | With response mode `dc_api.jwt` | Always |
| Platforms | Android | Android and iOS |
| Credo API | `agent.openid4vc` in `@credo-ts/openid4vc` | `agent.mdoc` in `@credo-ts/core`, since Credo 0.7.1 |

[OpenID4VC](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/openid4vc.md) and [ISO mdoc](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/mdoc.md) explain the protocols themselves.

## Platform support

Which browsers support the API, and which protocols they accept, differs per platform and changes quickly. Check the current support before you depend on it. At the time of writing:

| Platform | Protocols | How wallets take part |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Android | OpenID4VP and `org-iso-mdoc` | The wallet registers its credentials, with their claim values, in Credential Manager. A matcher compares each request with them in a sandbox, and the system picker shows the matching credentials. |
| iOS 26 and later | `org-iso-mdoc` only | The wallet is a document provider of the Identity Document Services framework. It registers only mdocs of a fixed set of document types, such as the mDL and the EU PID, and iOS matches requests on the document type alone. |

Chrome supports both protocols, and Safari only `org-iso-mdoc`. On desktop, the browser can pass the request to a phone nearby.

## Which should I use?

As a verifier:

| Choice | Default | When to pick the other |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Protocol | For mdocs, pass an OpenID4VP and an `org-iso-mdoc` request in one call, so wallets on both platforms can answer. For SD-JWT VCs, OpenID4VP. | `org-iso-mdoc` alone reaches wallets on both platforms without the OpenID4VC module, but misses Android wallets that only support OpenID4VP. |
| Signed requests | Unsigned. The wallet identifies you by the origin of your website, which the browser verified through its TLS certificate. | Sign when wallets or your ecosystem need to know who you are beyond the origin, for example a registered verifier. Use `x509_hash` for OpenID4VP, as HAIP does, and reader authentication for `org-iso-mdoc`. Some wallets only answer signed requests. |
| Response encryption (OpenID4VP) | `dc_api.jwt`. Only your backend can read the response, not the page and the browser it passes through. HAIP requires it. | `dc_api` only for testing. `org-iso-mdoc` always encrypts. |

As a wallet, support `org-iso-mdoc` for mdocs, as it's the only protocol iOS passes on, and OpenID4VP on Android for SD-JWT VCs and for verifiers that only send OpenID4VP. Credo answers signed and unsigned requests of both protocols, encrypted or not. HAIP also asks wallets to accept multi-signed OpenID4VP requests (`openid4vp-v1-multisigned`), which Credo doesn't support.

## Next steps

- [Building a verifier](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/dc-api/verifier.md): create the requests, call the API from a web page, and verify the response.
- [Building a wallet](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/dc-api/wallet.md): answer requests in a React Native wallet.

# Building a verifier

> Request credentials from a website with the W3C Digital Credentials API. A Credo backend creates OpenID4VP and ISO 18013-7 Annex C requests and verifies the response, and the web page calls the API in the browser.

A verifier for the Digital Credentials API has two parts: a Node.js backend with a Credo agent, which creates the requests and verifies the responses, and a web page that passes them through the browser. This page builds both. The example asks for the given name and age over 18 from an mDL, with OpenID4VP and with ISO 18013-7 Annex C (`org-iso-mdoc`) in one call, so wallets on Android and iOS can answer. [Digital Credentials API](https://credo.js.org/guides/protocols/dc-api.md) explains the flow and the choices.

## Set up the backend

```bash
npm install @credo-ts/core@^0.7.2 @credo-ts/node@^0.7.2 @credo-ts/openid4vc@^0.7.2 express
```

The agent also needs storage, see [Storage](https://credo.js.org/guides/agent-setup/storage.md). The backend creates the requests, verifies the responses, and serves the web page:

```ts
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { Agent, ClaimFormat, X509Module } from '@credo-ts/core'
import { agentDependencies } from '@credo-ts/node'
import { OpenId4VcModule } from '@credo-ts/openid4vc'
import express from 'express'

// The origin of the web page that calls the Digital Credentials API. This server serves the page.
const origin = 'http://localhost:4037'

const app = express()
// The web page, with the code from dc-api-verifier-browser.ts
app.use(express.static('public'))

const verifier = new Agent({
  config: {
    // Allows the http://localhost URLs of this example. Never enable this in production.
    allowInsecureHttpUrls: true,
  },
  dependencies: agentDependencies,
  modules: {
    ...storage, // Storage and key management, see Agent setup
    // Certificates (or root CAs) of the issuers you accept, as PEM or base64. For an mDL, the IACA certificates.
    x509: new X509Module({ trustedCertificates: [readFileSync('issuer-certificate.pem', 'utf8')] }),
    // Only needed for OpenID4VP. ISO 18013-7 Annex C uses `agent.mdoc`, which every agent has.
    openid4vc: new OpenId4VcModule({ app, verifier: { baseUrl: `${origin}/oid4vp` } }),
  },
})

await verifier.initialize()
const { verifierId } = await verifier.openid4vc.verifier.createVerifier()
```

- `origin` is the origin of the page that calls the API. Here the backend serves the page, so it's the backend's own origin.
